nodes.name: Partial Fourier transform (unitary side)
nodes.statement:
Let $v$ be a place of $F$. We define the
partial Fourier transform
\[
^\ddagger \colon \mathcal S(\mathbb L (F_v)) \otimes \mathcal S(\mathbb L (F_v))
\to \mathcal S(V^\vee(F_v))
\]
by
\[
    (\phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v})^\ddagger(z)
    = \int_{\mathbb L(F_v)} \phi_{1,v}(x' + x)
    \phi_{2,v}(x - x')
    \psi_v(-2\mathrm{Tr}_{E/F}\langle x', y\rangle)\,dx'
\]
for $z = x + y \in V^\vee$
with $x \in \mathbb L$ and $y \in \mathbb L^\vee$.
Here, $\langle -, -\rangle$ is the skew-hermitian form on $V^\vee$.
We define the global partial Fourier transform
$^\ddagger \colon \mathcal S(\mathbb L(\mathbb A_F)) \otimes \mathcal S(\mathbb L(\mathbb A_F)) \to \mathcal S(V^\vee(\mathbb A_F))$ using the same formula.
nodes.statement_short: The partial Fourier transform sends phi_1 x phi_2 on L x L to a Schwartz function on V^vee by integrating over L against psi.

nodes.name: Diagonal equivariance of the partial Fourier transform
nodes.statement:
( \overline{\omega(h)\phi_{1,v} } \otimes 
  \omega(h)\phi_{2,v})^\ddagger(z)= (\overline{\phi_{1,v}} 
  \otimes \phi_{2,v})^\ddagger(zh), \quad h \in \mathrm{U}(V)
  (F_v), \quad z \in V^\vee(F_v).

nodes.name: Reduction formula for products of theta series
nodes.statement:
For $\phi=(\phi_1 \otimes \phi_2)^\ddagger \in \mathcal{S}(V^\vee(\mathbb A_F))$ we have
\begin{equation}
\overline{ \Theta(g, \phi_1) }  \Theta(g, \phi_2) = \sum_{z \in V^\vee(E)} \phi(zg).
\end{equation}
Therefore, for $a \in H(F)$, we have 
\[
\overline{\Theta(h_1, \phi_1)}  \Theta(h_2, \phi_2)  = \sum_{z \in V^\vee(E)} ( \overline{ \omega(h_2^{-1}ah_1) \phi_1} \otimes  \phi_2)^\ddagger (zh_2).
\]
conclusions: \overline{ \Theta(g, \phi_1) }  \Theta(g, \phi_2) = \sum_{z \in V^\vee(E)} \phi(zg).
nodes.statement_short: A product of a conjugate theta series and a theta series is a single theta sum of the partial Fourier transform.
nodes.label: key:reduction

nodes.name: Theta product reduction identity
nodes.statement: \overline{ \Theta(g, \phi_1) }  \Theta(g, \phi_2) = \sum_{z \in V^\vee(E)} \phi(zg).

nodes.name: Set [Y_rss] for representatives R
nodes.statement: [Y_{\textnormal{rss}}]=(R \times V^\vee)_{\textnormal{rss}} / \sim

nodes.name: Good test function (unitary side)
nodes.statement:
An element $(f = \otimes_{v} f_v, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2 = \otimes_{v}  (\phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v} ))$ of $C_c^\infty(G(\mathbb A)) \times \mathcal{S}(\mathbb L(\mathbb A))^{\otimes 2}$ is called a
\emph{good test function} if it satisfies the following
properties.
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item There exists a finite place $v_1$ of
$F$ which is split in $E$ such that $f_{v_1}$ is a truncated matrix coefficient of a supercuspidal representation, that is, of
the form
\[
    f_{v_1}(g) = \widetilde{f_{v_1}}(g) 
    \cdot \mathbf{1}_{G(F_{v_1})^1}(g),
\]
where $\widetilde{f_{v_1}}$ is a matrix coefficient of
a supercuspidal representation of $G(F_{v_1})$, and
\[
    G(F_{v_1})^1 = \{g \in G(F_{v_1}) : 
    \lvert \det g \rvert_{v_1} =  1  \}.
\]

\item There exists a finite place $v_2$ of $F$
which is split in $E$ such that
$f_{v_2}$ is supported on the regular
semisimple $H(F_{v_2}) \times H(F_{v_2})$-orbits 
of $G(F_{v_2})$, and if $[\zeta, z] \in (R^V\times V^\vee)$ and
\[
    f_{v_2}(h_1^{-1}\zeta h_2)
    (\overline{\omega
    (h_2^{-1}h_1)\phi_{1,v_2}} \otimes 
    \phi_{2,v_2})^\ddagger(zh_2)\neq 0
\]
for some $h_1, h_2 \in \mathrm{U}(V)(F_{v_2})$,
then $[\zeta, z] \in (R \times V^\vee)_{\textnormal{rss}}$.

\item For any place $v$ of $F$,
the function $f_v$ is supported on
\[
    \{\zeta \in G(F_v) : H(F_v) \zeta H(F_v)
    \text{ contains a normal element}\}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: A good unitary test function has a truncated supercuspidal matrix coefficient at v_1, regular semisimple support at v_2, and support on orbits containing normal elements.
nodes.label: def:ugood

nodes.name: Relative trace formula distribution J
Formula for J
Geometric decomposition of J (unitary side)
nodes.statement:
For a good test function $(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2)$, we have 
\[
    J(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2)= \sum_{[\zeta, z] \in [Y_{\textnormal{rss}}] 
    }
    \int_{H(\mathbb A)}\int_{H(\mathbb A)}
    f(h^{-1}_2 \zeta h_1)
    (\overline{\omega(h^{-1}_2h_1)\phi_1} \otimes \phi_2)^\ddagger(zh_2)\,dh_1\,dh_2,
\]
and both sides converge absolutely.
conclusions: both sides converge absolutely
nodes.statement_short: For good test functions J is an absolutely convergent sum over [Y_rss] of adelic orbital integrals involving the partial Fourier transform.
nodes.label: prop:udecomp

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.1.5
nodes.statement_short: Unfold the kernel over normal representatives and their stabilizers, replace the theta product by Xue's reduction formula, and refold over [Y_rss].

nodes.name: Unfold the kernel over representatives and apply the theta r
nodes.statement_short: Unfold the kernel over representatives and apply the theta reduction formula.

nodes.name: Integrate over [H] x [H] to get the decomposition.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate over [H] x [H] to get the decomposition.

nodes.name: Convergence from the regular semisimple support condition.
nodes.statement:
Both sides converge because of Definition 
\ref{def:ugood}\eqref{ursssupp} .
nodes.statement_short: Convergence from the regular semisimple support condition.

nodes.name: Local orbital integral (unitary side)
nodes.statement:
For regular semisimple $[\zeta, z] \in G(F_v) \times V_v^\vee$,
$f_v \in C_c^\infty(G(F_v))$, and
$\phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v} \in \mathcal S(\mathbb L(F_v))^{\otimes 2}$, 
define the \emph{(local) orbital integral} (cf. \cite[(4.1.2) and (4.1.4)]{Xue-GGP})
\begin{align*}
    &\mathrm{Orb}([\zeta, z], f_v, \phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v}) = \int_{H(F_v)}\int_{H(F_v)} f_v(h_1^{-1}\zeta h_2)
    ( \overline{\omega_v(h^{-1}_2h_1)\phi_{1,v}} \otimes \phi_{2,v})^\ddagger(zh_2)\, dh_1\, dh_2.
\end{align*}
nodes.label: defn: local orb: unitary side

nodes.name: Euler product decomposition of J
nodes.statement:
We have the decomposition
\[
    J(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2)
    = \sum_{[\zeta, z] \in [Y_{\textnormal{rss}}]}
    \Delta_H^{*,-2}
    \prod_v \mathrm{Orb}([\zeta, z], f_v, \phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v}).
\]
conclusions: J(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2) = \sum_{[\zeta, z] \in [Y_{\textnormal{rss}}]} \Delta_H^{*,-2} \prod_v \mathrm{Orb}([\zeta, z], f_v, \phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v}).
nodes.statement_short: J is a sum over [Y_rss] of products of local orbital integrals.

nodes.name: Weil representation R_mu and theta series Theta_mu (GL side)
nodes.label: defn theta series: GL side

nodes.name: Formula for R_mu
nodes.statement:
(R_\mu(g)\phi')(z) = \mu(\det g) \lvert \det g \rvert^{\frac12}
    \phi'(zg).

nodes.name: Formula for Theta_mu
nodes.statement: \Theta_\mu(s, g, \phi') = \sum_{z \in E_n \setminus \{0\}} (R_\mu(g) \phi')(z) \lvert \det g \rvert^{s-\frac 12}

nodes.name: Partial Fourier transform (GL side)
nodes.statement:
Let $v$ be a place of $F$. Define the partial Fourier transform
\[
^\dagger \colon \mathcal S(E_{v,n}) \to \mathcal S(F_{v,n} \times
F_v^{-,n})
\]
by
\[
    \phi_v'^\dagger(x, y) =
    \lvert j \rvert_v \int_{F_{v,n}} \phi_v'(x + jw^\vee) 
    \psi_v(jw^\vee y)\, dw^\vee.
\]
Here, the Haar measure is chosen to be the self-dual measure with respect to $\psi_v$.

nodes.name: Global partial Fourier transform (GL side)
nodes.statement:
We define the global partial Fourier transform
$$
^\dagger \colon \mathcal S(\mathbb A_{E,n}) \to  \mathcal S(\mathbb A_n \times \mathbb A^{-,n})
$$ using the same formulas.

nodes.name: H_10-equivariance of the GL partial Fourier transform
nodes.statement:
The first thing is for any $h \in H_{10}(F_v)=\mathrm{GL}_n(F_v)$
\[
(R_\mu(h)\phi')^\dagger(x, y) = \eta_{E/F}(\det h) \phi'^\dagger(xh, h^{-1}y).
\]
conclusions: (R_\mu(h)\phi')^\dagger(x, y) = \eta_{E/F}(\det h) \phi'^\dagger(xh, h^{-1}y).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.2.3 by Poisson summation
nodes.statement: The second thing is the following global reduction formula proved by the Possion summation formula.
nodes.statement_short: Poisson summation in the partial variable.

nodes.name: Global reduction formula (GL side)
nodes.statement:
For any $\phi' \in\mathcal{S}(\mathbb A_{E, n})$, we have 
\[
\sum_{v \in E_n} \phi'(v) = \sum_{(x, y) \in F_n \times F^{-,n}} \phi'^\dagger (x,y).
\]
conclusions: \sum_{v \in E_n} \phi'(v) = \sum_{(x, y) \in F_n \times F^{-,n}} \phi'^\dagger (x,y).
nodes.statement_short: Summing phi' over E_n equals summing its partial Fourier transform over F_n x F^{-,n} (Poisson summation).
nodes.label: key:reduction-GL

nodes.name: Theta_mu as a sum of partial Fourier transforms
nodes.statement:
Hence for any $a \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb A_E)$ and $h \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb A_F)$, we have
\begin{align*}
\Theta_\mu(ah, \phi') &=
\eta_{E/F}(\det a) \lvert \det h a \rvert^{\frac 12} \sum_{v \in E_n} \phi'(v h a) \\
&= \eta_{E/F}(\det h)^{-1} \sum_{(x, y)
\in F_n \times F^{-,n}} (R_\mu(ha) \phi')^\dagger (x, y)\\
&=
\sum_{(x, y) \in F_n \times F^{-,n}} (R_\mu(a) \phi')^\dagger (xh, h^{-1}y).
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Theta_mu(ah, phi') equals the sum over F_n x F^{-,n} of (R_mu(a)phi')^dagger(xh, h^{-1}y).

nodes.name: Good test function (GL side)
nodes.statement:
An element $(f' = \otimes_v f_v', \phi' = \otimes_v \phi'_v)$
of $C_c^\infty(G'(\mathbb A_F)) \times \mathcal S(\mathbb A_{E,n})$ is
called a \emph{good test function} if it satisfies the 
following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item There exists a finite place $v_1$ of
$F$ which is split in $E$ such that $f_{v_1}'$ is of
the form
\[
    f_{v_1}'(g) = \widetilde{f_{v_1}'}(g) 
    \cdot \mathbf{1}_{G^{\prime}(F_{v_1})^1}(g),
\]
where $\widetilde{f_{v_1}'}$ is a matrix coefficient of a
supercuspidal representation of $G'(F_{v_1})$, and
\[
    G'(F_{v_1})^1 = \{g \in G'(F_{v_1}) : \lvert \det g \rvert_{v_1} = 1 \}.
\]
\item There exists a finite
place $v_2$ of $F$ which is split in $E$ such that
$\widetilde f_{v_2}'$ is supported on the regular
semisimple $\mathrm{GL}_n(E_{v_2})$-orbits of $\textnormal{S}_n(K_{v_2})$,
and if $[\gamma, x, y] \in X$ and
\[
    \widetilde f_{v_2}'(g^{-1}\gamma \sigma_{E/F}(g))
    \overline{(R_{\mu_{v_2}}(g)\phi_{v_2}')^\dagger(x, y)} \neq 0
\]
for some $g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(E_{v_2})$, then $[\gamma, x, y] \in X_{\textnormal{rss}}$.

\item For all archimedean places $v$ of $F$, we have
$E_v = F_v \times F_v$, and $\phi_v'$ is a finite 
linear combination of functions of the form 
$\phi_{1,v}' \otimes \phi_{2,v}'$ where
$\phi_{1,v}', \phi_{2,v}' \in \mathcal S(F_{v,n})$.
\end{enumerate}
nodes.label: def:glgood

nodes.name: Notation eta_{L/K}(h)
nodes.statement: For $h_2' \in H_2(F)$, we write $\eta_{L/K}(h)=\eta_{L/K}(\det h)$.

nodes.name: Relative trace formula distribution I
nodes.statement:
For $f' \in C_c^\infty(G'(\mathbb A))$ and $\phi' \in
\mathcal S(\mathbb A_{E,n})$, define the distribution
\begin{equation}
   I(f', \phi') =
    \int_{[H_1]}\int_{[H_2]} K_{f'}(h_1, h_2) \overline{\Theta_\mu(h_1, \phi')}\eta_{L/K}(h_2)^{n+1}\, dh_1\,dh_2. 
\end{equation}
where 
$K_{f'}(h_1, h_2) = \sum_{\gamma \in G'(F)} f'(h_1^{-1} \gamma h_2).$

nodes.name: Formula for I
nodes.statement:
I(f', \phi') =
    \int_{[H_1]}\int_{[H_2]} K_{f'}(h_1, h_2) \overline{\Theta_\mu(h_1, \phi')}\eta_{L/K}(h_2)^{n+1}\, dh_1\,dh_2.

nodes.name: Local orbital integral (GL side)
nodes.label: defn: local orb GL side

nodes.name: Formula for the GL orbital integral
Equivariance of the GL orbital integral
nodes.statement:
Note that we have
\[
    \mathrm{Orb}([h_1^{-1}\xi h_2, xh_1, h_1^{-1}y],
    f_v', \phi_v')
    = \eta_{E_v/F_v}(h_1)\eta_{L_v/K_v}(h_2)^{n+1}
   \mathrm{Orb}([\xi, x, y], f_v', \phi_v') .
\]

nodes.name: Local character eta'_v
nodes.statement:
To make the orbital integrals only depend on $\gamma$
rather than a lifting $\xi$, we fix a character $\eta_v' \colon L_v^\times \to \mathbb C^\times$
satisfying $\eta_v'|_{K_v^\times} 
= \eta_{L_v/K_v}^{n+1}$.

nodes.name: Pushforward function f~'_v on S_{n,L/K}
nodes.statement:
Define a new function $\widetilde {f_v'}$ on $\mathrm{S}_{n,L/K}(F_v)$ by
\begin{equation} \widetilde {f_v'} (\gamma) \coloneqq
    \eta_v'(\xi)\int_{H_2(F_v)} f_v'(\xi h_2)
    \eta_{L_v/K_v}(h_2)^{n+1}\, dh_2.    
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Definition of f~'_v
nodes.statement:
\widetilde {f_v'} (\gamma) \coloneqq
    \eta_v'(\xi)\int_{H_2(F_v)} f_v'(\xi h_2)
    \eta_{L_v/K_v}(h_2)^{n+1}\, dh_2.
nodes.label: eq:ftilde

nodes.name: Simplified orbital integral on S_{n,L/K}
nodes.statement:
For $[\gamma, x, y] \in [X_{\textnormal{rss}}]$, define the orbital integral for $\widetilde f_v' \in C_c^\infty(\mathrm{S}_{n,L/K})$ and $\phi_v' \in \mathcal S(E_{v,n})$ as 
\[
    \mathrm{Orb}([\gamma, x, y], \widetilde f_v', \phi_v')
    = \int_{H_1(F_v)}
    \widetilde f_v'(h_1^{-1}\gamma \sigma_{L/K}(h_1) ) \overline{(R_{\mu_v}(h_1)\phi_v')^\dagger(x, y)}
    \eta_v'(h_1)\, dh_1.
\]
Note as $h \in H_1(F_v)$, we have $\sigma_{L/K}(h_1)=\sigma_{E/F}(h_1)$.
nodes.label: defn: semip orb int on GL side

nodes.name: Relation between the two GL orbital integrals
nodes.statement:
By definition, for $\xi \in G'(F)$ with
$\xi\sigma_{L/K}(\xi)^{-1} = \gamma$, we have
\[
    \mathrm{Orb}([\xi, x, y], f_v', \phi_v')
    = \eta_v'(\xi)^{-1}\cdot \mathrm{Orb}([\gamma, x, y], \widetilde f_v', \phi_v').
\]

nodes.name: Split case of the simplified orbital integrals
nodes.statement: We simplified the orbital integrals into the action of $H_{1}$ on $G'/H_2$. In the split case ($K=F \times F$), we are consider the $\sigma_{E/F}$-conjugacy action of $\mathrm{GL}_n(E)$ on $\mathrm{S}_{n,E/F} \times \mathrm{S}_{n, E/F}$. As $\mathrm{GL}_n(E)$ acts transitively on $\mathrm{S}_{n,E/F}$, we may choose a good representative $\xi \in \{1\} \times \mathrm{S}_{n,E/F}$, then we reduce to the action of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ on $\mathrm{S}_{n,E/F}$ by conjugacy.

nodes.name: Geometric decomposition of I (GL side)
nodes.statement:
For good test functions $(f', \phi')$, we have
\[
    I(f', \phi') = \Delta_{H_1}^{*,-1} \Delta_{H_2}^{*,-1} \sum_{[\gamma, x, y] \in [X_{\textnormal{rss}}]}
    \prod_v \mathrm{Orb}([\xi, x, y], f_v', 
    \phi_v'),
\]
where $\xi$ is an element of $\mathrm{GL}_n(L)$ such
that $\gamma = \xi\sigma_{L/K}(\xi)^{-1}$, and
the product of local orbital integrals does
not depend on the choice of $\xi$.
conclusions: the product of local orbital integrals does not depend on the choice of $\xi$
nodes.statement_short: For good test functions I is a sum over [X_rss] of products of local GL orbital integrals.
nodes.label: prop:gldecomp

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.2.9
nodes.statement_short: Fold the H_2-integral into a sum over S_n(K), unfold over normal representatives, expand Theta_mu via the GL reduction formula, and recombine.

nodes.name: Fold the kernel's H_2-integral into a sum over S_n(K).
nodes.statement_short: Fold the kernel's H_2-integral into a sum over S_n(K).

nodes.name: Unfold over representatives and expand the theta series via
nodes.statement_short: Unfold over representatives and expand the theta series via partial Fourier transforms.

nodes.name: Combine to get the decomposition of I.
nodes.statement_short: Combine to get the decomposition of I.

nodes.name: Determinant factor T_[delta,x,y]
Galois behaviour of T
nodes.statement:
Note that
\[
    \sigma_{L/E}(T_{[\delta, x, y]})
    = (\det \delta)^{-(n-1)} T_{[\delta, x, y]}.
\]

nodes.name: Normalized determinant factor lies in E
nodes.statement:
For $[\xi, x, y] \in \mathrm{GL}_n(L) \times F_n \times F^{-,n}$,
let $\gamma = \xi\sigma_{L/K}(\xi)^{-1}$
and $\delta = \gamma\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma)^{-1}$.
We have
\[
    \sigma_{L/E}(\det(\xi\sigma_{L/M}(\xi))^{-1}) = \det \delta\cdot \det(\xi\sigma_{L/M}(\xi))^{-1},
\]
so
\[
    \det(\xi\sigma_{L/M}(\xi))^{-(n-1)}T_{[\delta, x, y]}
    \in E.
\]

nodes.name: Transfer factor Omega
Equivariance of the transfer factor
nodes.statement:
\Omega([g^{-1}\xi h, xg, g^{-1}y]) 
    = \eta_{E/F}(g)\eta_{L/K}(h)^{n+1} \Omega([\xi, x, y])
nodes.label: eq:Omegainvariance

nodes.name: Normalized transfer factor omega
nodes.statement:
For $[\gamma, x, y] \in \textnormal{S}_{n,L/K} \times F_n
\times F^{-,n}$ with $\gamma$ normal, define normalized transfer factor
\[
    \omega([\gamma, x, y]) =
    \eta'(\xi)\Omega([\xi, x, y]),
\]
where $\xi$ is an element of $\mathrm{GL}_n(L)$ such
that $\gamma = \xi\sigma_{L/K}(\xi)^{-1}$.
This does not depend on the choice of $\xi$, and
satisfies
\[
    \omega([h^{-1}\gamma h, xh, h^{-1}y])
    = \eta_{E/F}(h)\omega([\gamma, x, y])
\]
for $h \in \mathrm{GL}_n(F)$.

nodes.name: (S,R^V)-smooth transfer
nodes.statement:
We say that $(f', \phi')$ and $\{(f^V, \phi_1^V \otimes 
\phi_2^V)\}_{V \in \mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)}$ are
\emph{$(S, R^V)$-smooth transfer} of each other if 
\[
    \mathrm{Orb}([\gamma, x, y], \widetilde f', \phi')
    = \omega([\gamma, x, y])
    \mathrm{Orb}([\zeta, z]^V, f^V, \phi_1^V\otimes \phi_2^V).
\]
for all matching $[\gamma, x, y] \in X_{\textnormal{rss}}$
and $[\zeta, z]^V \in Y_{\textnormal{rss}}^V$.
This is equivalent to
\[
    \mathrm{Orb}([\xi, x, y], f', \phi')
    = \Omega([\xi, x, y])
    \mathrm{Orb}([\zeta, z]^V, f^V, \phi_1^V\otimes \phi_2^V),
\]
where $\gamma = \xi\sigma_{L/K}(\xi)^{-1}$. 
In particular, it does not depend on the choice of
$\eta'$.
nodes.statement_short: Test functions are smooth transfers if matching GL and unitary orbital integrals agree up to the transfer factor.
nodes.label: defn: smooth transfer

nodes.name: Kottwitz element
nodes.statement:
We say that an element $\xi \in \mathrm{GL}_n(L)$ is \emph{Kottwitz}
if either of the following holds.
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item We have
\[
    \xi = c_{n-1}(\xi\sigma_{L/E}(\xi)^{-1})^{n-1}
    + \cdots + c_0
\]
for some $c_0, \dots, c_{n-1} \in \mathcal O_L$.
\item 
There does not exist $g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(L)$ such that
$g^{-1}\xi\sigma_{L/E}(\xi)^{-1} g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$.
\end{enumerate}
nodes.label: def:kottwitzgeneral

nodes.name: k-Kottwitz pair
nodes.statement:
Let $\varpi_F$ be a uniformizer of $F$, and let
$k \ge 0$ be an integer. We say that an element
$(\xi_1, \xi_2) \in \mathrm{GL}_n(E) \times \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$
is \emph{$k$-Kottwitz} if 
\[
    \xi_1 = c_{n-1}(\xi_1\xi_2^{-1})^{n-1}
    + \cdots + c_0
\]
for some $c_0 \in 1 + \varpi_F^k \mathcal O_E$ 
and $c_1, \dots, c_{n-1} \in \varpi_F^k \mathcal O_E$.
nodes.label: def:kkottwitz

nodes.name: Integrality properties of Kottwitz elements
nodes.statement:
Suppose $\xi \in \mathrm{GL}_n(L)$ is Kottwitz, and
an element of either $\textnormal{S}_{n,L/K}$ or $\mathrm{U}(V)(K)$.
\begin{enumerate}[\normalfont(1)]
    \item If $g^{-1}\xi\sigma_{L/E}(\xi)^{-1} g
    \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$ for $g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(L)$, then
    $g^{-1}\xi g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$.
    
    \item If $h_1^{-1}\xi h_2 \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$ for 
    $h_1, h_2 \in \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$, then $h_2^{-1}h_1 \in 
    \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_E)$.
    
    \item Assume that $E/F$ is unramified.
 If $g^{-1}\xi\sigma_{E/F}(g)
    \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$ for $g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$, then
    $g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(F)\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_E)$.
\end{enumerate}
assumptions: Suppose $\xi \in \mathrm{GL}_n(L)$ is Kottwitz, and an element of either $\textnormal{S}_{n,L/K}$ or $\mathrm{U}(V)(K)$.

conclusions: $g^{-1}\xi g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$
$h_2^{-1}h_1 \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_E)$
$g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(F)\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_E)$

nodes.statement_short: For Kottwitz xi, integrality of the conjugated norm forces integrality of conjugated xi, of h_2^{-1}h_1, and (E/F unramified) g in GL_n(F)GL_n(O_E).
conclusions: $g^{-1}\xi g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$
$h_2^{-1}h_1 \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_E)$
$g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(F)\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_E)$
nodes.label: lem:kottwitzproperties

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1.3
nodes.statement:
Since $\xi$ is Kottwitz,
$g^{-1}\xi\sigma_{L/E}(\xi)^{-1} g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$ 
implies $g^{-1}\xi g \in \mathrm{Mat}_n(\mathcal O_L)$.
If $\xi \in \textnormal{S}_{n,L/K}$, then $\sigma_{L/E}(\xi)^{-1}
= \sigma_{L/M}(\xi)$, and if $\xi \in \mathrm{U}(V)(K)$,
we have $\sigma_{L/E}(\xi)^{-1} = \sigma_{L/E}(\xi^\ast)$.
In either case, $\det \xi \in \mathcal O_L$ implies
$\det(\sigma_{L/E}(\xi)^{-1}) \in \mathcal O_L$ as well.
Since $\det\xi \det(\sigma_{L/E}(\xi)^{-1}) 
\in \mathcal O_L^\times$, we have $\det \xi \in \mathcal O_L^\times$,
so $g^{-1}\xi g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$.
This proves \eqref{kot}.

\eqref{kot2} follows from the fact 
$h_1^{-1}\xi h_2 \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$ implies
$h_1^{-1}\xi\sigma_{L/E}(\xi)^{-1}
h_1 \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$, which implies $h_1^{-1}\xi h_1
\in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$ by \eqref{kot}.
\eqref{glkot1} follows from \eqref{kot2}
and the fact that if $g^{-1}\sigma_{E/F}(g)
\in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_E)$ for $g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$, then
$g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(F)\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_E)$ by 
\cite[Lemma~8.7]{Kottwitz1980}.
nodes.statement_short: Kottwitz polynomial expression gives integrality; a determinant argument upgrades to units; parts (2),(3) follow from (1) and Kottwitz's Lemma 8.7.

nodes.name: Kottwitz expression gives g^{-1} xi g integral.
nodes.statement:
Since $\xi$ is Kottwitz,
$g^{-1}\xi\sigma_{L/E}(\xi)^{-1} g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$ 
implies $g^{-1}\xi g \in \mathrm{Mat}_n(\mathcal O_L)$.
nodes.statement_short: Kottwitz expression gives g^{-1} xi g integral.

nodes.name: In both cases det(sigma(xi)^{-1}) is integral when det xi is
nodes.statement:
If $\xi \in \textnormal{S}_{n,L/K}$, then $\sigma_{L/E}(\xi)^{-1}
= \sigma_{L/M}(\xi)$, and if $\xi \in \mathrm{U}(V)(K)$,
we have $\sigma_{L/E}(\xi)^{-1} = \sigma_{L/E}(\xi^\ast)$.
In either case, $\det \xi \in \mathcal O_L$ implies
$\det(\sigma_{L/E}(\xi)^{-1}) \in \mathcal O_L$ as well.
nodes.statement_short: In both cases det(sigma(xi)^{-1}) is integral when det xi is.

nodes.name: det xi is a unit, proving (1).
nodes.statement:
Since $\det\xi \det(\sigma_{L/E}(\xi)^{-1}) 
\in \mathcal O_L^\times$, we have $\det \xi \in \mathcal O_L^\times$,
so $g^{-1}\xi g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$.
This proves \eqref{kot}.
nodes.statement_short: det xi is a unit, proving (1).

nodes.name: (2) follows from (1).
nodes.statement:
\eqref{kot2} follows from the fact 
$h_1^{-1}\xi h_2 \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$ implies
$h_1^{-1}\xi\sigma_{L/E}(\xi)^{-1}
h_1 \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$, which implies $h_1^{-1}\xi h_1
\in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$ by \eqref{kot}.
nodes.statement_short: (2) follows from (1).

nodes.name: (3) follows from (2) and Kottwitz's Lemma 8.7.
nodes.statement:
\eqref{glkot1} follows from \eqref{kot2}
and the fact that if $g^{-1}\sigma_{E/F}(g)
\in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_E)$ for $g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$, then
$g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(F)\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_E)$ by 
\cite[Lemma~8.7]{Kottwitz1980}.
nodes.statement_short: (3) follows from (2) and Kottwitz's Lemma 8.7.

nodes.name: Existence of Kottwitz lifts (E/F, K/F inert)
nodes.statement:
Assume that $E/F$ and $K/F$ are both inert.
Let $\gamma_0 \in \textnormal{S}_{n,L/K}$ be normal, and let
$\delta = \gamma_0\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma_0)^{-1}$.
Suppose there exists $g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(L)$ such that
$g^{-1}\delta g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_{L})$. 
Then there exists $\gamma \in \textnormal{S}_{n,L/K}$ with 
$\gamma\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma)^{-1} = \delta$ such
that $\gamma$ is Kottwitz.
assumptions: Assume that $E/F$ and $K/F$ are both inert.
Suppose there exists $g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(L)$ such that $g^{-1}\delta g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_{L})$.
conclusions: there exists $\gamma \in \textnormal{S}_{n,L/K}$ with $\gamma\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma)^{-1} = \delta$ such that $\gamma$ is Kottwitz
nodes.label: lem:kottwitzexist

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1.4
nodes.statement:
Since $K = E$, we have $L = E \times E$ 
  and $\gamma_0 = (\gamma_{01}, \sigma_{E/F}(\gamma_{01})^{-1})$
  for some $\gamma_{01} \in \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$.
  Then $\delta = (\delta_1, \delta_1^{-1})
  = (\gamma_{01}\sigma_{E/F}(\gamma_{01}),
  \sigma_{E/F}(\gamma_{01})^{-1}\gamma_{01}^{-1})$,
  and $\delta_1 \in \mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ since $\gamma_0$ is normal.
  The assumption that 
  $g^{-1}\delta g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_{L})$ for $g = (g_1, g_2) \in
  \mathrm{GL}_n(E) \times \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$ implies that
  $g_1^{-1} \delta_1 g_1
  \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_{E})$.
  By {\cite[Lemma 5.4]{TGGP-Wang}} (which is essentially
  {\cite[Lemma 8.8]{Kottwitz1980}}), there exists   
  $\gamma_1 \in \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$ with 
  $\gamma_1\sigma_{E/F}(\gamma_1) = \delta_1$
  such that
  \[
    \gamma_1 = 
    c_{n-1}(\gamma_1\sigma_{E/F}(\gamma_1))^{n-1} 
    + \cdots + c_0
  \]
  for $c_0, \dots, c_{n-1} \in \mathcal O_{E}$.
  Since the characteristic polynomial of
  $\gamma_{01}\sigma_{E/F}(\gamma_{01})$ has coefficients
  in $\mathcal O_{E}$, this implies that
  $\sigma_{E/F}(\gamma_1)^{-1}$ also has the above
  property,
  so $\gamma = (\gamma_1, \sigma_{E/F}(\gamma_1)^{-1})$
  is Kottwitz as an element of $\mathrm{GL}_n(L)$.
nodes.statement_short: Split L = E x E, reduce to delta_1 in GL_n(F) with integral conjugate, and apply Wang's/Kottwitz's Lemma to build a Kottwitz gamma.

nodes.name: Write gamma_0 and delta in coordinates of L = E x E; delta_1
nodes.statement:
Since $K = E$, we have $L = E \times E$

nodes.statement:
Assume that $K/F$ is split ($E/F$ may be ramified),

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1.5
nodes.statement:
In this case, we have $L = E \times E$ and 
$\gamma_0 = (\gamma_{01}, \gamma_{02})$ for some
$\gamma_{01}, \gamma_{02} \in \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$ satisfying
$\gamma_{01}\sigma_{E/F}(\gamma_{01}) 
= \gamma_{02}\sigma_{E/F}(\gamma_{02}) = 1$,
and $\delta = (\gamma_{01}\gamma_{02}^{-1},
\gamma_{02}\gamma_{01}^{-1})$.
Let $\gamma = (1, \gamma_{02}\gamma_{01}^{-1})$,
which is Kottwitz because
\[
    \gamma = (0, 1)\delta + (1, 0).
\]
In addition, $\gamma \in \textnormal{S}_{n,L/K}$ because
$\gamma_{01}$ and $\gamma_{02}$ commute, since
$\gamma$ is normal.
nodes.statement_short: Explicitly take gamma = (1, gamma_02 gamma_01^{-1}), which is a linear polynomial in delta.

nodes.name: Compatible sets of representatives
nodes.statement:
We say that sets of normal representatives (c.f. \ref{normal reps: unitary}, \ref{normal reps: GL side})
    $S$ and $R^V$ are \emph{compatible} if
    for all $\gamma \in S$, $\zeta \in R^V$,
    and $h \in \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$ such that
    \[
        h^{-1}\gamma\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma)^{-1} h =
        \zeta\sigma_{L/E}(\zeta)^{-1},
    \]
    we also have
    \[
        h^{-1}\gamma h = \zeta.
    \]
nodes.label: def:compatible

nodes.name: Compatibility transfers the Kottwitz property
nodes.statement:
It is clear that if $S$ and $R^V$ are compatible sets
of representatives,
and every element of $S$ is Kottwitz (resp. $k$-Kottwitz),
then every element of $R^V$ is Kottwitz (resp.
$k$-Kottwitz) as well.
assumptions: $S$ and $R^V$ are compatible sets of representatives
conclusions: every element of $R^V$ is Kottwitz (resp. $k$-Kottwitz) as well

nodes.name: Existence of compatible representatives
nodes.statement:
For every set of representatives $S$, there exists
a set of representatives $R^V$ which is
compatible with $S$.
conclusions: For every set of representatives $S$, there exists a set of representatives $R^V$ which is compatible with $S$.
nodes.label: lem:compatibleexist

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.1.7
nodes.statement:
Let $S$ be a set of normal representatives of the
regular semisimple $\mathrm{GL}_n(E)$-orbits of $\textnormal{S}_{n, L/K}$.
Recall that $R^V$ is a set of representatives
of the regular semisimple $\mathrm{U}(V)(F) \times
\mathrm{U}(V)(F)$-orbits of $\mathrm{U}(V)(K)$ which
contain a normal element.

Suppose $\zeta'$ is a normal element
of $\mathrm{U}(V)(K)$. 
We choose the representative of
$\mathrm{U}(V)(F)\zeta' \mathrm{U}(V)(F)$ as follows.
By Proposition \ref{lem:matching},
there exists $\gamma \in S$ such that 
\[
    h^{-1}\gamma\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma)^{-1} h
    = \zeta' \sigma_{L/E}(\zeta')^{-1}
\]
for some $h \in \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$.
Then by Lemma \ref{lem:normmatch} (1), 
$\zeta \coloneqq h^{-1}\gamma h$ is a normal
element of $\mathrm{U}(V)(K)$ which satisfies
$\zeta\sigma_{L/E}(\zeta)^{-1} =
\zeta'\sigma_{L/E}(\zeta')^{-1}$, so
$\zeta \in \mathrm{U}(V)(F)\zeta' \mathrm{U}(V)(F)$.

If $h'$ is another element of $\mathrm{GL}_n(E)$ such that
\[
     h'^{-1}\gamma\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma)^{-1} h'
    = \zeta\sigma_{L/E}(\zeta)
    = h^{-1}\gamma\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma)^{-1} h,
\]
then $h'^{-1}\gamma h' = h^{-1}\gamma h = \zeta$ because
the centralizer of $\gamma\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma)^{-1}$
is a torus which contains $\gamma$, by normality.
Thus, taking $\zeta$ to be the representative
of the orbit $\mathrm{U}(V)(F)\zeta' \mathrm{U}(V)(F)$, we obtain
a set of representatives $R^V$ compatible with $S$.
nodes.statement_short: For each normal unitary orbit choose zeta = h^{-1} gamma h via orbit matching and Lemma 2.4.8; torus centralizers make the choice independent of h.

nodes.statement_short: For Kottwitz gamma the unramified GL orbital integral reduces to a GL_n(F)-integral over conjugates of the norm.
nodes.label: lem:GLFLred

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2.1
nodes.statement:
Note that since $\gamma \in \textnormal{S}_{n,L/K}$ is normal, we have
\[
    g^{-1}\gamma\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma)^{-1} g \in
    \textnormal{S}_{n,L/K} \cap \textnormal{S}_{n, L/E}
\]
for all $g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(F)$.
By Lemma \ref{lem:kottwitzproperties} \eqref{glkot1}
and \eqref{kot}, for $g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$, we have 
$g^{-1}\gamma\sigma_{E/F}(g) \in \textnormal{S}_{n, \mathcal O_L/\mathcal O_K}$
if and only if $g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(F)\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_E)$
and $g^{-1}\gamma\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma)^{-1} g
\in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_L)$.

Since $\phi'$ is fixed by $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_E)$, we have
\begin{align*}
    \mathrm{Orb}([\gamma, x, y], \widetilde f', \phi')
    &= \int_{\mathrm{GL}_n(E)} \mathbf{1}_{\textnormal{S}_{n, \mathcal O_L/\mathcal O_K}}
    (g^{-1}\gamma \sigma_{E/F}(g)) \overline{(R_{\mu}(g)\phi')^\dagger(x, y)}
    \eta'(g)\, dg \\
    &= \int_{\mathrm{GL}_n(F)} \mathbf{1}_{\textnormal{S}_{n, \mathcal O_L/\mathcal O_K} \cap \textnormal{S}_{n, L/E}}
    (g^{-1} \gamma\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma)^{-1} g)
    \overline{(R_\mu(g)\phi')^\dagger(x, y)}\, dg \\
    &= \int_{\mathrm{GL}_n(F)} \mathbf{1}_{\textnormal{S}_{n, \mathcal O_L/\mathcal O_K} \cap
    \textnormal{S}_{n, L/E}}
    (g^{-1}\gamma\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma)^{-1} g)
    (\phi')^\dagger(xg, g^{-1} y) \eta_{E/F}(g) \,dg.
\end{align*}
In the second line, we used the fact that
$\eta'|_{F^\times} = 1$ for all choices of $\eta'$,
and $\eta'|_{\mathcal O_E^\times} = 1$
since $\eta'$ is unramified, so $\eta'|_{E^\times} = 1$.
In the third line, we used the fact that
\[
    (R_\mu(g)\phi')^\dagger(x, y) = (\phi')^\dagger(xg,
    g^{-1}y)\eta_{E/F}(g)
\]
for all $g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(F)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2.2
nodes.statement:
Note that 
\[
    h^{-1}\zeta\sigma_{L/E}(\zeta)^{-1} h \in 
    \mathrm{U}(V^+)(K) \cap \textnormal{S}_{n, L/E}
\]
for all $h \in \mathrm{U}(V^+)(F)$.
By Lemma \ref{lem:kottwitzproperties} \eqref{kot2}, 
for $g, h \in \mathrm{U}(V^+)(F)$, we have
$g^{-1}\zeta h \in \mathrm{U}(V^+)(\mathcal O_K)$ if and only if
$h^{-1} g \in \mathrm{U}(V^+)(\mathcal O_F)$ and 
$h^{-1}\zeta h \in \mathrm{U}(V^+)(\mathcal O_K)$.
By Lemma \ref{lem:kottwitzproperties} \eqref{kot},
$h^{-1}\zeta h \in \mathrm{U}(V^+)(\mathcal O_K)$ if and only if
$h^{-1} \zeta \sigma_{L/E}(\zeta)^{-1} h \in
\mathrm{U}(V^+)(\mathcal O_K) \cap \textnormal{S}_{n, L/E}$.

Thus, since $\overline{\phi_1} \otimes \phi_2$ is fixed by 
$\mathrm{U}(V^+)(\mathcal O_F) \times \mathrm{U}(V^+)(\mathcal O_F)$,
we have
\begin{align*}
    \mathrm{Orb}([\zeta, z]^{V^+}, f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2) &= 
    \int_{\mathrm{U}(V^+)(F)} \mathbf{1}_{\mathrm{U}(V^+)(\mathcal O_K)}
    (h^{-1}\zeta h) 
    (\overline{\phi_1} \otimes \phi_2)^\ddagger(zh)\, dh \\
    &= \int_{\mathrm{U}(V^+)(F)} \mathbf{1}_{\mathrm{U}(V^+)(\mathcal O_K) \cap \textnormal{S}_{n, L/E}}
    (h^{-1} \zeta\sigma_{L/E}(\zeta)^{-1} h) 
    (\overline{\phi_1} \otimes \phi_2)^\ddagger(zh)\, dh.
    \qedhere
\end{align*}

nodes.statement:
Suppose $[\gamma, x, y] \in X_{\textnormal{rss}}$

        \omega([\gamma, x, y])
        \mathrm{Orb}([\zeta, z], f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2).

    If $[\gamma, x, y]$ matches with
    $[\zeta, z] \in Y_{\textnormal{rss}}^{V^-}$, with
    $\gamma$ and $\zeta$ Kottwitz, then
    \[
        \mathrm{Orb}([\gamma, x, y], \widetilde f', \phi') = 0.
    \]

nodes.name: Split smooth transfer
nodes.statement:
We say that a test function $(f', \phi') 
\in C_c^\infty(\mathrm{GL}_n(K) \times
\mathrm{GL}_n(K)) \otimes \mathcal S_n(E_n)$ and
a test function $(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2) \in
C_c^\infty(\mathrm{GL}_n(K)) \otimes \mathcal S(F_n)^{\otimes 2}$
are \emph{split smooth transfer} of each other 
if there exists $f_1', f_2' \in C_c^\infty(\mathrm{GL}_n(K))$
such that 
\[
    f = f_1' \ast f_2'^\vee, \quad
    f' = f_1' \otimes f_2', \quad
    \phi' = \phi_1 \otimes \overline{\phi_2},
\]
where $f^\vee$ is the function given by
$f^\vee(g) \coloneqq f(g^{-1})$ and $\ast$
denotes convolution.

nodes.name: Fourier--Jacobi orbital integral (GL side)
nodes.statement:
For $[(\xi_1, \xi_2), x, y] \in (G'(F)
\times F_n \times F^{-,n})_{\textnormal{rss}}$, 
$f' \in C_c^\infty(G'(F))$, 
and $\phi' \in \mathcal S(E_n)$, define
\begin{align*}
    &\mathrm{Orb}^{\textnormal{FJ}}([(\xi_1, \xi_2), x, y], f', \phi')\\
    &= \int_{\mathrm{GL}_n(E)}
    \iint_{\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\times\mathrm{GL}_n(F)}
    f'(g^{-1}(\xi_1, \xi_2)(h_1, h_2))
    \overline{(R_\mu(\xi_1^{-1} g)\phi')^\dagger
    (x, y)}
    \eta_{E/F}(h_1h_2)^{n+1}\,dh_1\,dh_2\,dg.
\end{align*}
Note that this orbital integral satisfies
\[
    \mathrm{Orb}^{\textnormal{FJ}}([g^{-1}(\xi_1, \xi_2)(h_1, h_2), xh_1,
    h_1^{-1}y])
    = \eta_{E/F}(h_1)^n\eta_{E/F}(h_2)^{n+1}
    \mathrm{Orb}^{\textnormal{FJ}}([(\xi_1, \xi_2), x, y])
\]
for $g \in H_1(F)$, $(h_1, h_2) \in H_2(F)$.

nodes.name: Fourier--Jacobi transfer factor
nodes.statement:
For $[(\xi_1, \xi_2), x, y] \in G'(F) \times
F_n \times F^{-,n}$, define transfer factor
\[
    \Omega^{\textnormal{FJ}}([(\xi_1, \xi_2), x, y])
    = \Omega([(1, \xi_1^{-1}\xi_2), x, y]).
\]
Note that by \eqref{eq:Omegainvariance}, this
transfer factor satisfies
\begin{align*}
    \Omega^{\textnormal{FJ}}([g^{-1}(\xi_1, \xi_2)(h_1, h_2),
    xh_1, h_1^{-1}y])
    &= \Omega([(1, h_1^{-1}\xi_1^{-1}\xi_2 h_2),
    xh_1, h_1^{-1} y]) \\
    &= \Omega([h_1^{-1}(1, \xi_1^{-1}\xi_2)
    (h_1, h_2), xh_1, h_1^{-1}y]) \\
    &= \eta_{E/F}(h_1)^n\eta_{E/F}(h_2)^{n+1}
    \Omega^{\textnormal{FJ}}([(\xi_1, \xi_2), x, y])
\end{align*}
for $g \in H_1(F)$, $(h_1, h_2) \in H_2(F)$.

    =

    \mathrm{Orb}^{\textnormal{FJ}}([(\zeta_1, \zeta_2), z]^V, f^V, 
    \phi_1^V \otimes \phi_2^V)
\]
for all $[(\xi_1, \xi_2), x, y] \in

and $[(\zeta_1, \zeta_2), z]^V 
\in (G(F) \times V^\vee)_{\textnormal{rss}}$ which match 
in the sense that
\[
    [(\xi_1^{-1}\xi_2)\sigma_{E/F}(\xi_1^{-1}\xi_2)^{-1},
x, y].h = [\zeta_1^{-1}\zeta_2, z, z^\ast]
\]
for some $h \in \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$.
The other direction also holds.

    \eta_{E/F}(h)^{n+1}\, dh
\]
for $\xi \in \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$ such that $\gamma

\[

    \gamma_2 \gamma_1^{-1}), x, y].h
    = [(\zeta_1 \zeta_2^{-1}, \zeta_2 \zeta_1^{-1}),

\]

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.4.5
nodes.statement:
Since \eqref{eq:transferexistence} does not
depend on the choice of $\eta'$ (although
both $\widetilde f'$ and 
$\omega([(\gamma_1, \gamma_2), x, y])$ do), 
for convenience, we assume that $\eta_1' = \eta_2'$.
Let $\xi_1, \xi_2, \xi \in \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$ be such
that $\gamma_1 = \xi_1\sigma_{E/F}(\xi_1)^{-1}$,
$\gamma_2 = \xi_2\sigma_{E/F}(\xi_2)^{-1}$,
and $\gamma_1^{-1}\gamma_2 = \xi\sigma_{E/F}(\xi)^{-1}$.
The transfer factor then satisfies
\begin{align}
    \omega([(\gamma_1, \gamma_2), x, y])
    &= \eta_1'(\xi_1\xi_2)
    \eta_{E/F}(\xi_2\sigma_{E/F}(\xi_1)\xi^{-1})^{-(n-1)}\Omega([(1, \xi), x, y])\nonumber\\
    &= \eta_1'(\xi_1\sigma_{E/F}(\xi_1)^{-1})
    \eta_1'(\xi)
    \Omega([(1, \xi), x, y])\nonumber\\
    &= \eta_1'(\gamma_1) \eta_1'(\xi)
    \Omega^{\textnormal{FJ}}([(1, \xi), x, y]). \end{align}

Let $\{(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2)\}_{V \in 
\mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)}$ be a collection of test
functions on the unitary side which matches
with $(f', \phi')$ as in Theorem
\ref{thm:FJtransfer}.
Suppose $f^V = f_1^V \otimes f_2^V$ for
$f_i^V \in C_c^\infty(\mathrm{U}(V)(F))$.
For $m \ge 1$ an integer, let
\[
    K_m = 1 + \varpi_F^m \mathrm{Mat}_n(\mathcal O_E).
\]
Since $\widetilde f_i'$ and $f_i^V$ are
compactly supported locally constant functions,
there exists $m \ge 1$ such that
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item
for all $\gamma \in \textnormal{S}_{n,E/F}$ and 
$g \in K_m \cap (\textnormal{S}_{n,E/F})\gamma^{-1}$,
we have
\[
    \widetilde f_1'(g\gamma) = \widetilde f_1'(\gamma),\quad
    \widetilde f_2'(g\gamma) = \widetilde f_2'(\gamma);
\]   

\item
for all $V \in \mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)$, 
$\zeta \in \mathrm{U}(V)(F)$, and 
$g \in K_m \cap \mathrm{U}(V)(F)$, we have
\[
    f_1^V(g\zeta) = f_1^V(\zeta),\quad
    f_2^V(g\zeta) = f_2^V(\zeta);
\]

\item $\eta_1'(g) = 1$ for all $g \in K_m$.
\end{enumerate}

Then let $k \ge 0$ be an integer with the following
properties.
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item
If 
\[
    g^{-1}\gamma_1 \sigma_{E/F}(g) \in 
    \mathrm{Supp}(\widetilde f_1'), \quad
    g^{-1}\gamma_2\sigma_{E/F}(g) \in \mathrm{Supp}(\widetilde f_2')
\]
for $k$-Kottwitz $(\gamma_1, \gamma_2)
\in \textnormal{S}_{n,E/F} \times \textnormal{S}_{n,E/F}$
and $g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$, then 
$g^{-1}\gamma_1 g \in K_m$.

\item 
For all $V \in \mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)$, if 
\[
    g^{-1}\zeta_1 h \in \mathrm{Supp}(f_1^V),\quad
    g^{-1}\zeta_2 h \in \mathrm{Supp}(f_2^V)
\]
for $k$-Kottwitz $(\zeta_1, \zeta_2)
\in \mathrm{U}(V)(F) \times \mathrm{U}(V)(F)$ and
$g, h \in \mathrm{U}(V)(F)$, 
then $g^{-1}\zeta_1 g \in K_m$.
\end{enumerate}
Indeed, since $\mathrm{Supp}(\widetilde f_i')$ 
and $\mathrm{Supp}(f_i)$ are compact subsets of $\mathrm{GL}_n(E)$,
we may choose $k \ge m$ such that
\[
    \varpi_F^k (\mathrm{Supp}(\widetilde f_1')\mathrm{Supp}(\widetilde
    f_2')^{-1})^i \subseteq \varpi_F^m \mathrm{Mat}_n(\mathcal O_E)
\]
and
\[
    \varpi_F^k (\mathrm{Supp}(f_1)\mathrm{Supp}(f_2)^{-1})^i
    \subseteq \varpi_F^m \mathrm{Mat}_n(\mathcal O_E)
\]
for $1 \le i \le n - 1$.
Then $k$ satisfies the desired properties because
for $k$-Kottwitz $(\gamma_1, \gamma_2)$, we have
\[
    g^{-1}\gamma_1 g
    = c_{n-1}(g^{-1}\gamma_1\gamma_2^{-1} g)^{n-1}
    + \cdots + c_0
\]
with $c_0 \in 1 + \varpi_F^k\mathcal O_E$
and $c_1, \dots, c_{n-1} \in \varpi_F^k\mathcal O_E$,
and similarly for $k$-Kottwitz $(\zeta_1, \zeta_2)$.

Then $k$ and the test functions 
$\{(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2)\}_{V \in \mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)}$ satisfy the
properties required in the proposition. 
Indeed, suppose that $(\gamma_1, \gamma_2)$
is normal, i.e., $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$
commute, and $k$-Kottwitz. Since
we also assumed that $\eta_1' = \eta_2'$, we have
\begin{align*}
&\mathrm{Orb}([(\gamma_1, \gamma_2), x, y], \widetilde f', \phi') \\
&= \int_{\mathrm{GL}_n(E)} 
\widetilde f_1'(g^{-1}\gamma_1 \sigma_{E/F}(g)) 
\widetilde f_2'(g^{-1}\gamma_2 \sigma_{E/F}(g))
\overline{(R_\mu(g)\phi')^\dagger(x, y)}
\eta_1'(g)\eta_2'(g)\,dg\\
&= \int_{\mathrm{GL}_n(E)}
\widetilde f_1'(g^{-1}\sigma_{E/F}(g))
\widetilde f_2'(g^{-1}\gamma_1^{-1}\gamma_2\sigma_{E/F}(g))
\overline{(R_\mu(g)\phi')^\dagger(x, y)}
\eta_1'(g)\eta_2'(g)\, dg \\
&= \eta_2'(\xi)
\int_{\mathrm{GL}_n(E)}\iint_{\mathrm{GL}_n(F) \times \mathrm{GL}_n(F)}
f_1'(g^{-1}h_1) f_2'(g^{-1}\xi h_2)
\overline{(R_\mu(g)\phi')^\dagger(x, y)}
\eta_{E/F}(h_1h_2)^{n+1}\,dh_1\,dh_2\,dg\\
&= \eta_1'(\xi) \cdot
\mathrm{Orb}^{\textnormal{FJ}}([(1, \xi), x, y], f', \phi')
\end{align*}
where $\xi \in \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$ such that
$\gamma_1^{-1}\gamma_2 = \xi\sigma_{E/F}(\xi)^{-1}$.
On the other hand, if $(\zeta_1, \zeta_2)$
is normal and $k$-Kottwitz, then
\begin{align*}
&\mathrm{Orb}([(\zeta_1, \zeta_2), z]^V, f^V, \phi_1^V \otimes \phi_2^V)\\
&= \iint_{\mathrm{U}(V)(F)\times \mathrm{U}(V)(F)}
f_1^V(g^{-1}\zeta_1 h)f_2^V(g^{-1}\zeta_2 h)
(\overline{\omega_{\psi,\mu}(h^{-1}g)\phi_1^V} \otimes \phi_2^V)^\ddagger(zh)\,dg\,dh\\
&= \iint_{\mathrm{U}(V)(F) \times \mathrm{U}(V)(F)}
f_1^V(g^{-1}h)f_2^V(g^{-1}\zeta_1^{-1}\zeta_2 h)
(\overline{\omega_{\psi,\mu}(h^{-1}g)\phi_1^V} \otimes \phi_2^V)^\ddagger(zh)\,dg\,dh\\
&= \mathrm{Orb}^{\textnormal{FJ}}([(1, \zeta_1^{-1}\zeta_2), z]^V, f^V,
\phi_1^V \otimes \phi_2^V).
\end{align*}

It is clear that if $[(\gamma_1, \gamma_2), x, y]$ and
$[(\zeta_1, \zeta_2), z]^V$ are regular semisimple 
and match in the sense of the proposition
statement, then $[(1, \xi), x, y]$ and 
$[(1, \zeta_1^{-1}\zeta_2), z]^V$
match as in Theorem \ref{thm:FJtransfer}.
Thus, since $\{(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2)\}_{V \in \mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)}$ is a smooth
transfer of $(f', \phi')$ for the Fourier--Jacobi
orbital integrals, we have
\begin{align*}
\mathrm{Orb}([(\gamma_1, \gamma_2), x, y], \widetilde f', \phi') 
&= \eta_1'(\xi)\Omega^{\textnormal{FJ}}([(1, \xi), x, y])
\mathrm{Orb}([(\zeta_1, \zeta_2), z]^V, f^V, \phi_1^V \otimes \phi_2^V)\\
&= \omega([(\gamma_1, \gamma_2), x, y])
\mathrm{Orb}([(\zeta_1, \zeta_2), z]^V, f^V, \phi_1^V \otimes \phi_2^V),
\end{align*}
where the last equality follows from \eqref{eq:fjtf}
and the assumption \eqref{item:eta}.

The proof for the other direction is the same.

\[

\]

compactly supported locally constant functions,

    f_2^V(g\zeta) = f_2^V(\zeta);
\]

\item $\eta_1'(g) = 1$ for all $g \in K_m$.

nonarchimedean places
of $F$ which are split in $K$.

nodes.name: k-Kottwitz at a K-split place
nodes.statement:
For each $1 \le i \le m$, 
let $u_i$ and $w_i$ be the places of $K$ lying above 
$v_i$. We identify $L_{v_i} = L_{u_i} \times L_{w_i}$
with $E_{v_i} \times E_{v_i}$, and say an
element of $\mathrm{GL}_n(L_{v_i})$ is $k$-Kottwitz if it is
$k$-Kottwitz in the sense of Definition 
\ref{def:kkottwitz}.

nodes.name: Global Kottwitz representatives
nodes.statement:
Let $k \ge 0$ be an integer.
Suppose $\gamma_0 \in \textnormal{S}_{n,L/K}$ is
regular semisimple and normal, and let $\delta
= \gamma_0\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma_0)^{-1}$. 
Then there exists $\gamma \in \textnormal{S}_{n,L/K}$ with
$\gamma\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma)^{-1} = \delta$,
such that $\gamma$ is Kottwitz at all places $v$ of $F$ 
which are inert in $E$ and unramified in $K$, and
$k$-Kottwitz at $v_1, v_2, \dots, v_m$.
assumptions: Suppose $\gamma_0 \in \textnormal{S}_{n,L/K}$ is regular semisimple and normal, and let $\delta = \gamma_0\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma_0)^{-1}$.
conclusions: there exists $\gamma \in \textnormal{S}_{n,L/K}$ with $\gamma\sigma_{L/E}(\gamma)^{-1} = \delta$, such that $\gamma$ is Kottwitz at all places $v$ of $F$ which are inert in $E$ and unramified in $K$, and $k$-Kottwitz at $v_1, v_2, \dots, v_m$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.1.1
nodes.statement:
Let $L'$ be the centralizer of $\delta$ in
$\mathrm{Mat}_n(L)$. 
Since $\delta$ is regular semisimple,
$L'$ is the commutative $L$-subalgebra of $\mathrm{Mat}_n(L)$ generated by
$\delta$. 
Note that $\sigma_{L/E}$ and $\sigma_{L/K}$
act on $L'$, since $\delta\sigma_{L/E}(\delta)
= \delta\sigma_{L/K}(\delta) = 1$.
Let $E'$ and $K'$ denote the $\sigma_{L/E}$ and
$\sigma_{L/K}$-fixed elements of
$L'$, respectively, and let $F' = E' \cap K'$. 

Let $\Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$ be the set of places $v \neq
v_1, \dots, v_m$ of $F$ which are inert in $E$ and unramified in $K$, such that
\[
    g^{-1}\delta g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_{L_v})
\]
for some $g \in \mathrm{GL}_n(L_v)$.
For $v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$, the characteristic 
polynomial of $\delta$ has coefficients in $\mathcal O_{L_v}$,
so $\delta \in \mathcal O_{L_v'}$. Note if $v \not \in \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$ is inert in $E$ and unramified in $K$ and $v \not = v_1, \hdots, v_m$, then $\gamma$ is automatically Kottwitz at $v$.

By Lemmas \ref{lem:kottwitzexist} and
\ref{lem:kkottwitzexist}, for each 
$v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$, there exists Kottwitz
$\gamma_v \in L_v'$ with 
$\gamma_v \sigma_{L'/K'}(\gamma_v) = 1$ and
$\gamma_v\sigma_{L'/E'}(\gamma_v)^{-1} = \delta$.
Since $\delta \in \mathcal O_{L_v'}$ as noted above,
by definition of $\gamma_v$ being Kottwitz, 
$\gamma_v \in \mathcal O_{L_v'}$.
In addition, by Lemma \ref{lem:kkottwitzexist},
for each $1 \le i \le m$,
there exists $\gamma_{v_i} \in L_{v_i}'$ with 
$\gamma_{v_i}\sigma_{L'/K'}(\gamma_{v_i}) = 1$ and
$\gamma_{v_i}\sigma_{L'/E'}(\gamma_{v_i})^{-1} = \delta$,
such that $\gamma_{v_i}$ is both Kottwitz
and $k$-Kottwitz.

By Lemma \ref{lem:kottwitzapprox}, there exists an
integer $m_v \ge 0$ for each $v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$
such that if $\gamma \in L_v'$ satisfies
\[
    \gamma - \gamma_v \in \varpi_{F_v}^{m_v}
    \mathcal O_{L_v'},
\]
then $\gamma$ is Kottwitz.
Also, there exist integers $m_{v_1}, \dots, m_{v_i}
\ge 0$ such that if $\gamma \in L_{v_i}'$ such that
\[
    \gamma - \gamma_{v_i} \in \varpi_{F_{v_i}}^{m_{v_i}}
    \mathcal O_{L_{v_i}'},
\]
then $\gamma$ is both Kottwitz and $k$-Kottwitz.
Furthermore, from the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:kottwitzapprox}, we see that we can take 
$m_v = 0$ for all but finitely many $v$.

Let $\Sigma = \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}} \cup
\{v_1, \dots, v_m\}$.
Let $\Sigma_{\text{f}}$ be a finite subset of
$\Sigma$ such that for all $v \in \Sigma - \Sigma_{\text{f}}$,
we have $v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$,
$\gamma_0 \in \mathcal O_{L_v'}^\times$, and $m_v = 0$.
Note that for all $v \in \Sigma $, we have 
$\gamma_v\gamma_0^{-1} \in E_v'$ and 
$\gamma_v\gamma_0^{-1}\sigma_{E'/F'}
(\gamma_v\gamma_0^{-1}) = 1$, 
so there exists $a_v \in \mathcal O_{E_v'}$ such that
\[
    \gamma_v = a_v^{-1} \gamma_0 \sigma_{E'/F'}(a_v).
\]  
Furthermore, for $v \in \Sigma - \Sigma_{\text{f}}$,
we have $\gamma_v\gamma_0^{-1} \in \mathcal O_{E_v'}^\times$
and the extension $E_v'/F_v'$ is unramified, 
so we can assume $a_v \in \mathcal O_{E_v'}^\times$.

For each $v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}$, let $\varepsilon_v > 0$
be an integer such that
\begin{equation} \varpi_{F_v}^{\varepsilon_v} a_v^{-1}
    \in \varpi_{F_v}\mathcal O_{E_v'}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation} \varpi_{F_v}^{\varepsilon_v} a_v^{-2}\gamma_0
   \in \varpi_{F_v}^{m_v}\mathcal O_{L_v'}.
\end{equation}
Since $\Sigma - \Sigma_{\text{f}} \subseteq \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$,
the set of places of $E'$ lying above an element of 
$\Sigma - \Sigma_{\text{f}}$ has Dirichlet density $0$, so
by Lemma \ref{lem:aapprox}, there exists
$a \in E'$ such that 
\begin{equation} a - a_v \in \varpi_{F_v}^{\varepsilon_v} \mathcal O_{E_v'}
\end{equation}
for all $v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}$, and $a \in \mathcal O_{E_v'}^\times$
for $v \in \Sigma - \Sigma_{\text{f}}$.

Let
\[
    \gamma = a^{-1}\gamma_0\sigma_{E'/F'}(a).
\]
Then for $v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}$, we have
$aa_v^{-1} \in \mathcal O_{E_v'}^\times$ by \eqref{eq:orda}
and \eqref{eq:aminusav}. Also recall that 
$a_v \in \mathcal O_{E_v'}$, so by \eqref{eq:aminusav}
and \eqref{eq:ordgamma}, we have
\begin{align*}
    \gamma - \gamma_v &= \gamma_0(a^{-1}\sigma_{E'/F'}(a) 
    - a_v^{-1}\sigma_{E'/F'}(a_v)) \\
    &= a^{-1}a_v^{-1}\gamma_0(a_v\sigma_{E'/F'}(a)
    - a\sigma_{E'/F'}(a_v)) \in \varpi_{F_v}^{\varepsilon_v} 
    a_v^{-2}\gamma_0 \mathcal O_{E_v'} \subseteq
    \varpi_{F_v}^{m_v}\mathcal O_{L_v'}.
\end{align*}
In addition, for $v \in \Sigma - \Sigma_{\text{f}}$, 
we have
\[
    \gamma - \gamma_v = \gamma_0(a^{-1}\sigma_{E'/F'}(a) 
    - a_v^{-1}\sigma_{E'/F'}(a_v)) \in \varpi_{F_v}^{m_v}\mathcal O_{L_v'}
\]
since $m_v = 0$, $\gamma_0 \in \mathcal O_{L_v'}^\times$,
and $a, a_v \in \mathcal O_{E_v'}^\times$.
Thus, by the construction of the $m_v$, this means
that $\gamma$ is Kottwitz at all $v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$ and
both Kottwitz and $k$-Kottwitz at $v = v_1, \dots, v_m$.
nodes.statement_short: Build local Kottwitz solutions gamma_v (Lemmas 4.1.4, 4.1.5), note small perturbations stay Kottwitz (Lemma 5.1.2), and approximate all of them by one global a in E' (Lemma 5.1.3).

nodes.name: Introduce the centralizer algebra L' of delta and its fixed
nodes.statement:
Let $L'$ be the centralizer of $\delta$ in
$\mathrm{Mat}_n(L)$. 
Since $\delta$ is regular semisimple,
$L'$ is the commutative $L$-subalgebra of $\mathrm{Mat}_n(L)$ generated by
$\delta$. 
Note that $\sigma_{L/E}$ and $\sigma_{L/K}$
act on $L'$, since $\delta\sigma_{L/E}(\delta)
= \delta\sigma_{L/K}(\delta) = 1$.
Let $E'$ and $K'$ denote the $\sigma_{L/E}$ and
$\sigma_{L/K}$-fixed elements of
$L'$, respectively, and let $F' = E' \cap K'$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the centralizer algebra L' of delta and its fixed subalgebras E', K', F'.

\]

nodes.statement_short: Define the finite-type set Sigma_in of inert places with integral conjugates; delta is integral there.

By Lemmas \ref{lem:kottwitzexist} and
\ref{lem:kkottwitzexist}, for each 
$v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$, there exists Kottwitz
$\gamma_v \in L_v'$ with 
$\gamma_v \sigma_{L'/K'}(\gamma_v) = 1$ and
$\gamma_v\sigma_{L'/E'}(\gamma_v)^{-1} = \delta$.
Since $\delta \in \mathcal O_{L_v'}$ as noted above,
by definition of $\gamma_v$ being Kottwitz, 
$\gamma_v \in \mathcal O_{L_v'}$.
In addition, by Lemma \ref{lem:kkottwitzexist},
for each $1 \le i \le m$,
there exists $\gamma_{v_i} \in L_{v_i}'$ with 
$\gamma_{v_i}\sigma_{L'/K'}(\gamma_{v_i}) = 1$ and
$\gamma_{v_i}\sigma_{L'/E'}(\gamma_{v_i})^{-1} = \delta$,
such that $\gamma_{v_i}$ is both Kottwitz
and $k$-Kottwitz.
nodes.statement_short: Local lemmas give Kottwitz (and k-Kottwitz) local solutions gamma_v.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.1.2: m_v-neighbourhoods of gamma_v stay (k-)Kottwitz
nodes.statement:
By Lemma \ref{lem:kottwitzapprox}, there exists an
integer $m_v \ge 0$ for each $v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$
such that if $\gamma \in L_v'$ satisfies
\[
    \gamma - \gamma_v \in \varpi_{F_v}^{m_v}
    \mathcal O_{L_v'},
\]
then $\gamma$ is Kottwitz.
Also, there exist integers $m_{v_1}, \dots, m_{v_i}
\ge 0$ such that if $\gamma \in L_{v_i}'$ such that
\[
    \gamma - \gamma_{v_i} \in \varpi_{F_{v_i}}^{m_{v_i}}
    \mathcal O_{L_{v_i}'},
\]
then $\gamma$ is both Kottwitz and $k$-Kottwitz.
Furthermore, from the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:kottwitzapprox}, we see that we can take 
$m_v = 0$ for all but finitely many $v$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.1.2: m_v-neighbourhoods of gamma_v stay (k-)Kottwitz; m_v = 0 for almost all v.

nodes.name: Openness of the k-Kottwitz condition
nodes.statement:
Let $v$ be a finite place of $L$, and let $k \ge 0$ be
an integer. Let $L_v'$ be an \'etale $L_v$-algebra
of dimension $n$.
Suppose $\delta \in L_v'$ generates $L_v'$ as an
$L_v$-algebra. 
There exists an integer $m = m(\delta, k)$ such that if 
\[
    \xi = c_{n-1}\delta^{n-1} + \cdots + c_0
\]
for some $c_0 \in 1 + \varpi_{L_v}^k\mathcal O_{L_v}$
and $c_1, \dots, c_{n-1} \in \varpi_{L_v}^k\mathcal O_{L_v}$,
and $\xi' \in L_v'$ satisfies 
$\xi' - \xi \in \varpi_{L_v}^m \mathcal O_{L_v'}$, then
\[
    \xi' = c_{n-1}'\delta^{n-1} + \cdots + c_0
\]
for some $c_0' \in 1 + \varpi_{L_v}^k\mathcal O_{L_v}$
and $c_1', \dots, c_{n-1}' \in \varpi_{L_v}^k\mathcal O_{L_v}$ 
as well.
assumptions: Let $v$ be a finite place of $L$, and let $k \ge 0$ be an integer.
nodes.statement_short: Elements close enough to a k-Kottwitz polynomial in delta are again k-Kottwitz polynomials in delta.
nodes.label: lem:kottwitzapprox

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.1.2
nodes.statement:
Let $p(X) \in L_v[X]$ be the minimal polynomial of 
$\delta$, so $L_v' = L_v[X]/(p(X))$. 
Let $\sigma_1, \dots, \sigma_n$ be the $n$
distinct maps of $L_v$-algebras $L_v' \to \overline{L_v}$,
where $\overline{L_v}$ denotes an algebraic closure of $L_v$.

Let $m = m(\delta)$ be an integer such that
\begin{equation} \varpi_{L_v}^m \cdot \begin{pmatrix}
        \sigma_1(\delta)^{n-1} & \cdots & 1 \\
        \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
        \sigma_n(\delta)^{n-1} & \cdots & 1
    \end{pmatrix}^{-1} 
    \in \varpi_{L_v}^k \mathrm{Mat}_n(\mathcal O_{\overline{L_v}}).
\end{equation} 
Note that the above matrix is invertible because 
$p(X)$ has $n$ distinct roots.

Now suppose $\xi' - \xi \in \varpi_{L_v}^m\mathcal O_{L_v'}$.
This implies 
\begin{equation} \sigma_i(\xi') - \sigma_i(\xi) \in \varpi_{L_v}^m
    \mathcal O_{\overline{L_v}}
\end{equation}
for $1 \le i \le n$.
Since $\delta$ generates $L_v'$, we know that
\[
    \xi' = c_{n-1}'\delta^{n-1} + \cdots + c_0'
\]
for some $c_0',\dots, c_{n-1}' \in L_v$.
We have
\[
    \sigma_i(\xi') = c_{n-1}'\sigma_i(\delta)^{n-1} + \cdots + c_0'
\]
for $1 \le i \le n$, so
\begin{align*}
    \begin{pmatrix}
        c_{n-1}' \\ \vdots \\ c_0' 
    \end{pmatrix} &= 
    \begin{pmatrix}
        \sigma_1(\delta)^{n-1} & \cdots & 1 \\
        \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
        \sigma_n(\delta)^{n-1} & \cdots & 1
    \end{pmatrix}^{-1} 
    \begin{pmatrix}
        \sigma_1(\xi') \\ \vdots \\ \sigma_n(\xi')
    \end{pmatrix} \\
    &= \begin{pmatrix}
        \sigma_1(\delta)^{n-1} & \cdots & 1 \\
        \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
        \sigma_n(\delta)^{n-1} & \cdots & 1
    \end{pmatrix}^{-1} 
    \begin{pmatrix}
        \sigma_1(\xi') - \sigma_1(\xi) \\ \vdots \\ \sigma_n(\xi') - \sigma_n(\xi)
    \end{pmatrix} +
    \begin{pmatrix}
        c_{n-1} \\ \vdots \\ c_0,
    \end{pmatrix}
\end{align*}
where the second equality follows from the analogous
formula for $\prescript{\top}{}{}{(c_{n-1}, \dots, c_0)}$.
Then the assumptions that $c_0 \in 1 + \varpi_{L_v}^k
\mathcal O_{L_v}$ and $c_1, \dots, c_{n-1} \in 
\varpi_{L_v}^k\mathcal O_{L_v}$, combined with \eqref{eq:m} and
\eqref{eq:sigdiff}, imply that 
$c_0' \in (1 + \varpi_{L_v}^k\mathcal O_{\overline{L_v}}) \cap L_v
= 1 + \varpi_{L_v}^k\mathcal O_{L_v}$ and $c_1', \dots, c_{n-1}'
\in (\varpi_{L_v}^k\mathcal O_{\overline{L_v}}) \cap L_v 
= \varpi_{L_v}^k\mathcal O_{L_v}$ as well.
nodes.statement_short: Recover polynomial coefficients by inverting the Vandermonde matrix of the embeddings of delta; choose m so the inverse times varpi^m is divisible by varpi^k.

nodes.name: Approximation avoiding a density-zero set
nodes.statement:
Let $E'$ be a number field. Let $\Sigma_0$
be a set of finite primes of $E'$ with Dirichlet density
$0$, and let $\Sigma_{\textnormal{f}}$ be finite set of finite primes
which is disjoint from $\Sigma_0$.
For each $v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal f}$, let $\varepsilon_v$ 
be an integer, and let $a_v$ be an element of 
$E_v'^\times$.
Then there exists $a \in E'^\times$
such that $a \in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$ for all $v \in \Sigma_0$, and
\[
    a - a_v \in \varpi_{E'_v}^{\varepsilon_v} \mathcal O_{E'_v}
\]
for all $v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal{f}}$.
assumptions: Let $\Sigma_0$ be a set of finite primes of $E'$ with Dirichlet density $0$
let $\Sigma_{\textnormal{f}}$ be finite set of finite primes which is disjoint from $\Sigma_0$.
For each $v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal f}$, let $\varepsilon_v$ be an integer, and let $a_v$ be an element of $E_v'^\times$.
conclusions: there exists $a \in E'^\times$ such that $a \in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$ for all $v \in \Sigma_0$, and \[ a - a_v \in \varpi_{E'_v}^{\varepsilon_v} \mathcal O_{E'_v} \] for all $v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal{f}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Weak approximation at finitely many places while staying a unit on a density-zero set of primes.
nodes.label: lem:aapprox

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.1.3
nodes.statement:
First, we note that there exists $c \in E'^\times$ 
such that $c^{-1} a_v\in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$ for all 
$v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}$ and $c \in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$ 
for all $v \in \Sigma_0$. Indeed, consider the 
fractional ideal
\[
    \mathfrak n = \prod_{v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal{f}}} \mathfrak p_v^{\mathrm{ord}_v(a_v)},
\]
where $\mathfrak p_v$ denotes the prime ideal of $\mathcal O_{E'_v}$
corresponding to $v$. Since $\Sigma_0 \cup \Sigma_{\text{f}}$ 
has Dirichlet density $0$, there exists a prime ideal
$\mathfrak q$ in the same ideal class as $\mathfrak n$.
Let $c$ be such that $c \mathfrak q = \mathfrak n$.
Then $c$ satisfies the required property.

Since $\Sigma_{\text{f}}$ is finite, by weak
approximation, there exists $a' \in E'^\times$ such that
\[  
    a' - c^{-1} a_v \in \varpi_{E'_v}^{\max\{1,
    \varepsilon_v - \mathrm{ord}_v(a_v)\}} \cdot \mathcal O_{E'_v}
\]
for all $v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}$.
Since $c^{-1} a_v \in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$ for
$v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}$,
clearly this implies $a' \in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$
for $v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}$. 

Let $\mathfrak m$ be the ideal
\[
    \mathfrak m = \prod_{v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}} 
    \mathfrak p_v^{\max\{0,
    \varepsilon_v - \mathrm{ord}_v(a_v)\}}.
\]
As noted above, the fractional ideal
$(a')$ is coprime to $\mathfrak m$. Thus, the set of prime
ideals of $\mathcal O_{E'}$ in the same ray class
modulo $\mathfrak m$ as $(a')$ has positive Dirichlet density,
so there exists $\mathfrak p$ in this ray class
which is not an element of $\Sigma_0$.

Let $b \in E'_{\mathfrak m, 1}$ be such that $(ba') = \mathfrak p$.
This means $b$ is an element of $E'$ such that
\[
    b - 1 \in \varpi_{E'_v}^{\max\{0,
    \varepsilon_v - \mathrm{ord}_v(a_v)\}} \cdot \mathcal O_{E'_v}
\]
for all $v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}$. 
We claim that $a = cba'$
satisfies the requirements of the lemma.

Indeed, for all $v \in \Sigma_0$,
we have $a \in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$ since 
$(c^{-1} a) = \mathfrak p$ is a prime ideal not contained in $\Sigma_0$, and $c \in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$.
In addition, for $v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}$, we have
\begin{align*}
    a - a_v &= ca'(b - 1) + c(a' - c^{-1}a_v) \\
    &= ca_v^{-1}(a'a_v(b - 1) + a_v(a' - c^{-1}a_v))
    \in
    \varpi_{E'_v}^{\varepsilon_v} \mathcal O_{E'_v},
\end{align*}
since $a_v(b - 1), a_v(a' - c^{-1}a_v) \in 
\varpi_{E'_v}^{\varepsilon_v} \mathcal O_{E'_v}$ and 
$a', ca_v^{-1} \in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$.
nodes.statement_short: Normalize by c from a prime in the ideal class of prod p_v^{ord a_v}, weakly approximate by a', then use Chebotarev density in a ray class to pick b with (ba') prime outside Sigma_0.

nodes.name: Find c normalizing the valuations of a_v, using a prime in t
nodes.statement:
First, we note that there exists $c \in E'^\times$ 
such that $c^{-1} a_v\in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$ for all 
$v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}$ and $c \in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$ 
for all $v \in \Sigma_0$. Indeed, consider the 
fractional ideal
\[
    \mathfrak n = \prod_{v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal{f}}} \mathfrak p_v^{\mathrm{ord}_v(a_v)},
\]
where $\mathfrak p_v$ denotes the prime ideal of $\mathcal O_{E'_v}$
corresponding to $v$. Since $\Sigma_0 \cup \Sigma_{\text{f}}$ 
has Dirichlet density $0$, there exists a prime ideal
$\mathfrak q$ in the same ideal class as $\mathfrak n$.
Let $c$ be such that $c \mathfrak q = \mathfrak n$.
Then $c$ satisfies the required property.
nodes.statement_short: Find c normalizing the valuations of a_v, using a prime in the ideal class (density argument).

nodes.name: Weak approximation gives a' close to c^{-1}a_v, hence a unit
nodes.statement:
Since $\Sigma_{\text{f}}$ is finite, by weak
approximation, there exists $a' \in E'^\times$ such that
\[  
    a' - c^{-1} a_v \in \varpi_{E'_v}^{\max\{1,
    \varepsilon_v - \mathrm{ord}_v(a_v)\}} \cdot \mathcal O_{E'_v}
\]
for all $v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}$.
Since $c^{-1} a_v \in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$ for
$v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}$,
clearly this implies $a' \in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$
for $v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Weak approximation gives a' close to c^{-1}a_v, hence a unit at Sigma_f.

nodes.name: Ray classes mod m have positive density, so pick a prime p o
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathfrak m$ be the ideal
\[
    \mathfrak m = \prod_{v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}} 
    \mathfrak p_v^{\max\{0,
    \varepsilon_v - \mathrm{ord}_v(a_v)\}}.
\]
As noted above, the fractional ideal
$(a')$ is coprime to $\mathfrak m$. Thus, the set of prime
ideals of $\mathcal O_{E'}$ in the same ray class
modulo $\mathfrak m$ as $(a')$ has positive Dirichlet density,
so there exists $\mathfrak p$ in this ray class
which is not an element of $\Sigma_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Ray classes mod m have positive density, so pick a prime p outside Sigma_0 in the ray class of (a').

nodes.name: Take b in the ray group with (ba') = p.
nodes.statement:
Let $b \in E'_{\mathfrak m, 1}$ be such that $(ba') = \mathfrak p$.
This means $b$ is an element of $E'$ such that
\[
    b - 1 \in \varpi_{E'_v}^{\max\{0,
    \varepsilon_v - \mathrm{ord}_v(a_v)\}} \cdot \mathcal O_{E'_v}
\]
for all $v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Take b in the ray group with (ba') = p.

nodes.name: Verify a = cba' satisfies the requirements.
nodes.statement:
We claim that $a = cba'$
satisfies the requirements of the lemma.

Indeed, for all $v \in \Sigma_0$,
we have $a \in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$ since 
$(c^{-1} a) = \mathfrak p$ is a prime ideal not contained in $\Sigma_0$, and $c \in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$.
In addition, for $v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}$, we have
\begin{align*}
    a - a_v &= ca'(b - 1) + c(a' - c^{-1}a_v) \\
    &= ca_v^{-1}(a'a_v(b - 1) + a_v(a' - c^{-1}a_v))
    \in
    \varpi_{E'_v}^{\varepsilon_v} \mathcal O_{E'_v},
\end{align*}
since $a_v(b - 1), a_v(a' - c^{-1}a_v) \in 
\varpi_{E'_v}^{\varepsilon_v} \mathcal O_{E'_v}$ and 
$a', ca_v^{-1} \in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$.
nodes.statement_short: Verify a = cba' satisfies the requirements.

nodes.name: Claim a = cba' works; it is a unit on Sigma_0.
nodes.statement:
We claim that $a = cba'$
satisfies the requirements of the lemma.

Indeed, for all $v \in \Sigma_0$,
we have $a \in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$ since 
$(c^{-1} a) = \mathfrak p$ is a prime ideal not contained in $\Sigma_0$, and $c \in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$.
nodes.statement_short: Claim a = cba' works; it is a unit on Sigma_0.

nodes.name: At Sigma_f, a - a_v has the required valuation.
nodes.statement:
In addition, for $v \in \Sigma_{\text{f}}$, we have
\begin{align*}
    a - a_v &= ca'(b - 1) + c(a' - c^{-1}a_v) \\
    &= ca_v^{-1}(a'a_v(b - 1) + a_v(a' - c^{-1}a_v))
    \in
    \varpi_{E'_v}^{\varepsilon_v} \mathcal O_{E'_v},
\end{align*}
since $a_v(b - 1), a_v(a' - c^{-1}a_v) \in 
\varpi_{E'_v}^{\varepsilon_v} \mathcal O_{E'_v}$ and 
$a', ca_v^{-1} \in \mathcal O_{E'_v}^\times$.
nodes.statement_short: At Sigma_f, a - a_v has the required valuation.

nodes.name: Right translation action R
nodes.statement:
For any reductive group $G$ over $F$, let $R$ denote the right translation action of
$G(\mathbb A)$ on $L^2(G(F)\backslash G(\mathbb A))$.

nodes.name: Cuspidal test function
nodes.statement:
For a place $v$ of $F$ and $f_{v} \in C_c^\infty(G(F_v))$, we say that $f_v$ is  cuspidal if for all parabolic $P=MN$ of $G_{F_v}$, we have
\[
    \int_{N(F_v)} f_v(nx) dn = 0, \quad \forall x \in G(F_v).
\]

nodes.name: Truncated supercuspidal matrix coefficients are cuspidal
nodes.statement: Note that any truncated matrix coefficient of a supercuspidal representation is cuspidal.
assumptions: any truncated matrix coefficient of a supercuspidal representation
conclusions: is cuspidal

nodes.name: Cuspidal local component forces cuspidal image
nodes.statement: It is well known that  If $f = f_{v_1}f^{v_1} \in C_c^\infty(G(\mathbb A))$ for, such that $f_{v_1}$ is cuspidal on $G(F_{v_1})$, then the image of $R(f)$ lies in $L^2_{\mathrm{cusp}}([G])$.
conclusions: the image of $R(f)$ lies in $L^2_{\mathrm{cusp}}([G])$

nodes.name: Spectral distribution J^V_pi
nodes.statement:
For any irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation 
    $\pi$ of $G^V(\mathbb A)$ and test function $(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2)$,
    define
    \[
        J^V_\pi(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2) 
        = \sum_{\varphi} \mathcal P(R(f)\varphi, \phi_1)\overline{\mathcal P(\varphi, \phi_2)},
    \]
    where the sum runs over an orthonormal basis of $\pi$.

nodes.name: Global zeta integral lambda and Flicker--Rallis period beta
nodes.label: def:globalzetaint

nodes.name: Global zeta integral lambda
nodes.statement: \lambda(s, \varphi, \mu, \phi') = \int\limits_{H_1(F)\backslash H_1(\mathbb A)} \varphi(g)\overline{\Theta_{\mu}(s, g, \phi')}\, dg

nodes.name: Flicker--Rallis period beta
nodes.statement:
\beta(\varphi) = \int\limits_{H_2(F)A_{G'}^\infty \backslash H_2(\mathbb A)}
    \varphi(h)\eta_{L/K}(\det h)^{n+1}\, dh.

nodes.name: Spectral distribution I_Pi
nodes.statement:
For any irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation $\Pi$ of $G'(\mathbb A)$ and test function $(f', \phi')$, define
\[
    I_\Pi(s, f', \phi') = \sum_\varphi \lambda(s, R(f')\varphi, \mu, \phi')
    \overline{\beta(\varphi)},
\]
   where the sum runs over an orthonormal basis of $\Pi$.

nodes.name: Spectral expansion of J
nodes.statement:
If the test function $(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2)$ is good (Definition \ref{def:ugood}), then 
    \[
        J^V(f , \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2)
        = \sum_\pi J^V_\pi(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2),
    \]
    where the sum runs over all irreducible cupsidal automorphic 
    representations of $G^V(\mathbb A)$.
    The right hand side is absolutely convergent.
conclusions: J^V(f , \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2) = \sum_\pi J^V_\pi(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2),
The right hand side is absolutely convergent.
nodes.label: prop:uspectral

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.2.4
nodes.statement:
Recall that
\begin{align*}
    J^V(f, \phi_1 \otimes \phi_2)
    = \int\limits_{H(F)\backslash H(\mathbb A)}
    \int\limits_{H(F)\backslash H(\mathbb A)}
    K_{f}(g, h)
    \overline{\Theta(g, \phi_1)}
    \Theta(h, \phi_2)\,dg\,dh.
\end{align*}
Since $f_{v_1}$ is a truncated matrix coefficient of a supercuspidal representation, the image of $R(f)$ lies in $L^2_{\operatorname{cusp}}([G^V])$.
Therefore,
\[
    K_f(x,y) = \sum_{\pi} K_{f,\pi}(x,y),
\]
where in the sum, $\pi$ runs through all cuspidal automorphic representations of $G^V(\mathbb A)$.
We have
\[
    K_{f, \pi}(g, h) =
    \sum_{\varphi}(R(f)\varphi)(g)
    \overline{\varphi(h)},
\]
where $\varphi$ runs over an orthonormal basis of $\pi$.
The proposition then follows.
The absolute convergence of the sum follows from
\cite[Proposition~A.1.2]{MR4332778}.
nodes.statement_short: The supercuspidal component makes R(f) cuspidal, so the kernel is a sum of cuspidal kernels; convergence by Proposition A.1.2 of [MR4332778].

nodes.name: Recall the definition of J^V.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the definition of J^V.

nodes.name: Supercuspidality at v_1 makes the kernel a sum over cuspidal
nodes.statement:

The absolute convergence of the sum follows from
\cite[Proposition~A.1.2]{MR4332778}.

nodes.name: Spectral expansion of I
nodes.statement:
If the test function $(f', \phi')$ is good (Definition \ref{def:glgood}), then
\[
    I(f', \phi') = \sum_{\Pi} I_\Pi(f', \phi')
\]
where the sum runs over all irreducible cuspidal 
automorphic representations of $G'(\mathbb A)$ with
central character trivial on $A_{G'}^\infty$.
The right hand side is absolutely convergent.
conclusions: I(f', \phi') = \sum_{\Pi} I_\Pi(f', \phi')
The right hand side is absolutely convergent.
nodes.label: prop:glspectral

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.2.5
nodes.statement:
Let
\[
    K_{\Pi}^0(x,y) = \int_{A_{G'}^\infty} K_{f,\Pi}(x,ay) da.
\]
Then we have
\[
    K_{\Pi}^0(x,y) = \sum_{\varphi} R(f)\varphi(x) 
    \overline{\varphi(y)},
\]
where the sum runs through the orthonormal basis of $\Pi$. The remaining are similar to the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:uspectral}.
nodes.statement_short: Average the cuspidal kernel over A_{G'}^infty and argue as for Proposition 5.2.4.

nodes.statement:

nodes.name: Linear independence of point evaluations with l^1 coefficients
assumptions: Let $X$ be a second countable compact Hausdorff space.
Given a sequence of distinct points $x_i$ of $X$ and a sequence $c_i$ of complex numbers such that \begin{equation*} \sum_{i=1}^{\infty} \lvert c_i \rvert < \infty. \end{equation*}
Suppose for any continuous function $f$ on $X$, we have \begin{equation*} \sum_{i=1}^{\infty} f(x_i)c_i = 0. \end{equation*}
conclusions: Then $c_i=0$ for any $i$.
nodes.label: lem:l^1_linearly_independent

nodes.name: Interpretation of the l^1 lemma
nodes.statement: The lemma formally says that the valuation functionals $f \mapsto f(x)$ on $C(X)$ as $x$ varies are “linear independent with $\ell^1$-coefficients”, where $C(X)$ is the Banach space of continuous functions on $X$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.3.1
nodes.statement_short: Isolate x_1 by a bump function supported where only the l^1-small tail lives; alternatively the coefficients define a Radon measure that must vanish.

nodes.name: WLOG show c_1 = 0.
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, we show that $c_1=0$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG show c_1 = 0.

nodes.name: Choose N so the tail of |c_i| is below epsilon.
nodes.statement_short: Choose N so the tail of |c_i| is below epsilon.

nodes.name: A bump function at x_1 avoiding x_2..x_N shows |c_1| < epsil
nodes.statement: Then pick a neighborhood $U$ of $x_1$ which only contains $x_i$ for $i>N$ and a function $f$ such that $0 \le f \le 1$, $f(x)=1$ and $f=0$ on $X \setminus U$, then we see that $\lvert c_1 \rvert < \varepsilon$.
nodes.statement_short: A bump function at x_1 avoiding x_2..x_N shows |c_1| < epsilon.

nodes.name: Hence c_1 = 0.
nodes.statement: Since $\varepsilon$ is arbitrary, we conclude that $c_1 = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence c_1 = 0.

nodes.name: Alternative: the coefficients form a Radon measure orthogona
nodes.statement: A more conceptual proof: it is easy to check that for a Borel set $Y$, $Y \mapsto \sum_{x_i \in Y} c_i$ defines a Radon measure $\mu$ on $X$, the condition says $\int_X f d \mu = 0$ for all continuous function of $X$. Therefore $\mu=0$. In particular, $\mu \left( \{ x_i\} \right) = c_i = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Alternative: the coefficients form a Radon measure orthogonal to C(X), hence zero.

nodes.name: Relative trace identity
nodes.statement:
Let $\Pi$ be the base change of $\pi$.
For good matching test functions $(f',\phi')$
and $\{(f^V,\phi_1^V \otimes \phi_2^V) \}_{V\in [\mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)]}$, we have
    \[
        I_\Pi(f', \phi') =
        \sum_{V \in [\mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)]} \sum_{\pi'} J_{\pi'}^V(f^V, \phi_1^V \otimes \phi_2^V),
    \]
where $\pi'$ runs over all irreducible cuspidal
automorphic representations of $\mathrm{U}(V)(\mathbb A_K)$
whose base change to $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb A_L)$ is also
$\Pi$.
assumptions: Let $\Pi$ be the base change of $\pi$.
conclusions: I_\Pi(f', \phi') = \sum_{V \in [\mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)]} \sum_{\pi'} J_{\pi'}^V(f^V, \phi_1^V \otimes \phi_2^V),
nodes.statement_short: For good matching test functions, the Pi-part of I equals the sum over V and over pi' with base change Pi of the unitary spectral terms.
nodes.label: prop:identity

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.3.3
nodes.statement:
From the geometric decomposition results in Proposition 
\ref{prop:gldecomp} and \ref{prop:udecomp},
the definition of matching
\ref{defn: smooth transfer}, and Propositions
\ref{prop:uspectral} and \ref{prop:glspectral},
we have 
\[
    \sum_{\Pi} I_\Pi(f', \phi') =
    \sum_{V \in [\mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)]} \sum_{\pi} 
    J^V_\pi(f^V, \phi_1^V \otimes \phi_2^V)
\]
where the first sum runs over cuspidal automorphic 
representations of $G'(\mathbb A)$ with central
character trivial on $A_{G'}^{\infty}$ and the second sum runs over
cuspidal automorphic representations of $G^V(\mathbb A)$ 
with central character trivial on $A_{G^V}^{\infty}$.

Let $\Sigma$ be the set of nonarchimedean places $v$
of $F$ which are split in $E$ and not equal to
$v_1, v_2$, such that
\begin{gather*}
    (f', \phi') = (\mathbf{1}_{\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_{L_v})}, \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal O_{E_v,n}}),\\ 
    (f^V, \phi_1^V \otimes \phi_2^V) =
    (\mathbf{1}_{\mathrm{U}(V)(\mathcal O_{K_v})}, \mathbf{1}_{\mathbb L(\mathcal O_{F_v})} \otimes
    \mathbf{1}_{\mathbb L(\mathcal O_{F_v})})
\end{gather*}
for all $V \in [\mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)]$.

Note that if $\pi_v$ is not unramified for some
$v \in \Sigma$, then both sides of the desired identity
are zero. Thus, we assume that $\pi_v$ is unramified
for all $v \in \Sigma$.
Let $\Lambda_{\Pi_{\Sigma}}$ denote the character
of the split spherical Hecke algebra
\[
    \bigotimes_{v \in \Sigma}'
    \mathcal H(\mathrm{GL}_n(L_v), \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_{L_v}))
\]
for $\Pi_\Sigma = \otimes_{v \in \Sigma}' \Pi_v$,
and similarly let $\lambda_{\pi_\Sigma}$ denote
the character of the split spherical Hecke algebra
\[
    \bigotimes_{v \in \Sigma}'
    \mathcal H(\mathrm{U}(V)(K_v), \mathrm{U}(V)(\mathcal O_{K_v}))
\]
for $\pi_\Sigma = \otimes_{v \in \Sigma}' \pi_v$.




From Proposition \ref{prop:splittransfer}, we have a
transfer map
\[
    b\colon \bigotimes_{v \in \Sigma}'
    \mathcal H(\mathrm{GL}_n(L_v), \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_{L_v})) \to
    \bigotimes_{v \in \Sigma}'
    \mathcal H(\mathrm{U}(V)(K_v), \mathrm{U}(V)(\mathcal O_{K_v}))
\]
given by $b(\alpha) = \alpha_1 \ast \alpha_2^\vee$
where $\alpha = \alpha_1 \otimes \alpha_2$.
Then we have
\[
   \lambda_{\pi_\Sigma}(b(\alpha))
   = \Lambda_{\operatorname{BC}(\pi)_\Sigma}(\alpha) 
\]
for all $\alpha \in \bigotimes_{v \in \Sigma}'
\mathcal H(\mathrm{GL}_n(L_v), \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_{L_v}))$.
The point is that $(f' \ast \alpha, \phi')$ and
$\{(f^V \ast b(\alpha), \phi_1^V
\otimes \phi_2^V)\}_{V \in [\mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)]}$
are also good matching test functions, so
\[
    \sum_\Pi I_\Pi(f', \phi') \Lambda_{\Pi_\Sigma}(\alpha)
    = \sum_{V \in [\mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)]} \sum_\pi
    J^V_\pi(f^V, \phi_1^V \otimes \phi_2^V)
    \Lambda_{\operatorname{BC}(\pi)_\Sigma}(\alpha).
\]

By \cite[Theorem~A]{ramakrishnan2018theorem},
if two cuspidal automorphic representations of
$\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb A_L)$ are isomorphic at almost all primes of
$L$ which are of degree $1$ over $F$, then they are
isomorphic.
This, combined with Lemma \ref{lem:l^1_linearly_independent} yields the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Equate geometric sides via matching, isolate the Pi-part by varying split spherical Hecke operators, and use strong multiplicity one (Ramakrishnan) with the l^1 independence lemma.

nodes.name: Geometric decompositions plus matching and spectral expansio
nodes.statement:
From the geometric decomposition results in Proposition 
\ref{prop:gldecomp} and \ref{prop:udecomp},

\ref{defn: smooth transfer}, and Propositions
\ref{prop:uspectral} and \ref{prop:glspectral},
we have 
\[
    \sum_{\Pi} I_\Pi(f', \phi') =
    \sum_{V \in [\mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)]} \sum_{\pi} 
    J^V_\pi(f^V, \phi_1^V \otimes \phi_2^V)
\]
where the first sum runs over cuspidal automorphic

nodes.statement_short: Geometric decompositions plus matching and spectral expansions equate the full spectral sums.
