nodes.name: Additive character psi_L
nodes.statement:
Let $\psi_L$ be the additive character of $\mathbb A_L/L$ 
given by
\[
    \psi_L(x) = \psi_E(j_K(x - \sigma_{L/E}(x))).
\]

nodes.name: Whittaker model W(Pi, psi_L)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal W(\Pi,\psi_L)$ be the Whittaker model of $\Pi$.

nodes.name: Borel B_n and unipotent radical N_n
nodes.statement:
Let $B_n$ be the standard upper triangular Borel of
$\mathrm{GL}_n$, and let $N_n$ be its unipotent radical.

nodes.name: Local Whittaker inner product
nodes.statement:
For $W_{1,v}, W_{2,v} \in \mathcal W(\Pi_v, \psi_{L_v})$, let
\[
    \langle W_{1,v}, W_{2,v} \rangle_v
    =
    \int\limits_{N_{n-1}(L_v) \backslash \mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(L_v)}
    W_{1,v}\left(\begin{pmatrix}
        g & \\ & 1
    \end{pmatrix}\right)
    \overline{W_{2,v}\left(\begin{pmatrix}
        g & \\ & 1
    \end{pmatrix}\right)}\,dg.
\]

nodes.name: Local zeta integral lambda_v and local period beta_v
Local zeta integral
nodes.statement:
\lambda_v(s, W_v, \mu_v, \phi_v')
    = \int\limits_{N_n(E_v)\backslash \mathrm{GL}_n(E_v)} W_v(g)
    \overline{\mu_v(\det g) \phi_v'(e_n g)} \lvert \det g \rvert^s\, dg.

nodes.name: Local Flicker--Rallis period
Role of epsilon_{n-1}
nodes.statement: Note that the matrix $\epsilon_{n-1}$ guarantees the integrand function is trivial on $N_{n-1}(K_v)$.

nodes.name: Local twisted GGP multiplicity one
nodes.statement: Let $\pi$ be a tempered cuspidal representation of $G^V(\mathbb A)$. Note that by the local twisted GGP conjecture \cite{le2025local}, for any place $v$, the vector space $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{U}(V)(F_v)}(\pi_v \otimes \overline{\omega_v}, \mathbb C)$ is at most one dimensional. Moreover, if the period $\mathcal{P}$ is non-trivial on $\pi$, then it is one-dimensional for any place $v$.
assumptions: Let $\pi$ be a tempered cuspidal representation of $G^V(\mathbb A)$.
conclusions: the vector space $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{U}(V)(F_v)}(\pi_v \otimes \overline{\omega_v}, \mathbb C)$ is at most one dimensional
if the period $\mathcal{P}$ is non-trivial on $\pi$, then it is one-dimensional for any place $v$

nodes.name: Local functional ell_v
nodes.statement:
If this is the case, which we will assume from now on, 
choose a generator $\ell_v$ of $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{U}(V)(F_v)}(\pi_v \otimes \overline{\omega_v}, \mathbb C)$.

nodes.name: Local relative character J_{pi_v}
nodes.statement:
For $f_v \in C_c^\infty(G^V(F_v))$ and $\phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v} \in \mathcal S(\mathbb L(F_v))^{\otimes 2}$, let
    \[
        J_{\pi_v}(f_v, \phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v})
        = \sum_{\varphi_v} \frac{\ell_v(\pi_v(f_v)\varphi_v, \phi_{1,v})\overline{\ell_v(\varphi_v, \phi_{2,v})}}
        {\langle \varphi_v, \varphi_v \rangle_v},
    \]
    where $\varphi_v$ runs over an orthogonal basis of $\pi_v$.

nodes.name: Local relative character I_{Pi_v}
nodes.statement:
For $f_v' \in C_c^\infty(G'(F_v))$ and $\phi_v' \in \mathcal S(E_{v,n})$, let
    \[
        I_{\Pi_v}(s, f_v', \phi_v')
        = \sum_{W_v} 
        \frac{\lambda_v(s, \Pi_v(f_v')W_v, \mu_v, \phi_v')\overline{\beta_v(W_v)}}
        {\langle W_v, W_v \rangle_v},
    \]
    where $W_v$ runs over an orthogonal basis
    of $\mathcal W(\Pi_v, \psi_{L_v})$.

nodes.name: Positive type test function
nodes.statement:
We say that a test function on the unitary side is of 
\emph{positive type} if it is of the form
$(f_v, \phi_v \otimes \phi_v)$, where $f_v =
f_0 \ast f_0^\star$ for some
$f_0 \in C_c^\infty(G(F_v))$, 
and $\phi_v \in \mathcal S(\mathbb L(F_v))$. 
Here, $\ast$ denotes convolution, and
$f_0^\star(g) \coloneqq \overline{f_0(g^{-1})}$.
We can similarly define positive type global test
functions.
nodes.label: def:postype

nodes.name: Convolution identity for local relative characters
Positivity of J_{pi_v} on positive type test functions
nodes.label: eq:postype

nodes.name: Nonvanishing via truncated matrix coefficients
nodes.statement:
Let $v$ be a nonarchimedean place of $F$.
    Assume that $\ell_v \neq 0$. There exists
    a test function $(f_v, \phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v})$
    such that 
    $J_{\pi_v}(f_v, \phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v}) \neq 0$ 
    and $f_v$ is a truncated matrix coefficient of $\pi_v$.
assumptions: Let $v$ be a nonarchimedean place of $F$.
conclusions: There exists a test function $(f_v, \phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v})$ such that $J_{\pi_v}(f_v, \phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v}) \neq 0$ and $f_v$ is a truncated matrix coefficient of $\pi_v$.
nodes.label: lem:matrixcoeff

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.4.6
nodes.statement:
The proof is the same as that of 
\cite[Lemma~6.14]{TGGP-Wang}.
nodes.statement_short: Same as Wang's Lemma 6.14.

nodes.name: Test functions with regular semisimple support
nodes.statement:
Let $v$ be a nonarchimedean place of $F$ which
is completely split in $L$ such that $\pi_v$
is supercuspidal. 
Assume that the distribution $J_{\pi_v}$ is
nonzero. 
Then there exists a test function $(f_v, \phi_v)$ 
with $\phi_v = \sum_{j=1}^r \phi_{1,v}^{(j)}
    \otimes \phi_{2,v}^{(j)}$
and an integer $k \ge 0$ such that 
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item $J_{\pi_v}(f_v, \phi_v)$ is nonzero;
\item $f_v$ is supported on the regular
semisimple locus of $G(F_v)$ under the
$H(F_v) \times H(F_v)$-action;
\item if $[\zeta, z] \in G(F_v) \times V_v^\vee$ is 
such that $\zeta$ is $k$-Kottwitz as an
element of $\mathrm{GL}_n(L_v)$ (in the sense of Definition 
\ref{def:kkottwitz}), and 
\[
    f_v(g^{-1}\zeta h)\left(\sum_{j=1}^r
    \phi_{2,v}^{(j)} \otimes \overline{\omega_v(h^{-1} g)\phi_{1,v}^{(j)}}\right)^\ddagger(zh) \neq 0
\] 
for some $g, h \in H(F_v)$, then $[\zeta, z] \in 
(G(F_v) \times V_v^\vee)_{\textnormal{rss}}$.
\end{enumerate}
assumptions: Let $v$ be a nonarchimedean place of $F$ which is completely split in $L$ such that $\pi_v$ is supercuspidal.
Assume that the distribution $J_{\pi_v}$ is nonzero.
nodes.statement_short: At a completely split supercuspidal place there are test functions with nonzero J_{pi_v} and regular semisimple support for k-Kottwitz representatives.
nodes.label: lem:rsssupp

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.4.7
nodes.statement:
This is shown in the proof of
{\cite[Lemma~6.13]{TGGP-Wang}}, once we identify
$G(F_v) = \mathrm{U}(V)(K_v)$ with $\mathrm{GL}_n(F_v) \times \mathrm{GL}_n(F_v)$.
Under this identification,
$\zeta$ being $k$-Kottwitz in the sense of Definition
\ref{def:kkottwitz} implies that $\zeta$ is
$k$-Kottwitz with respect to $\beta$
in the sense of \cite[Definition~4.10(2)]{TGGP-Wang}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to Wang's Lemma 6.13 after identifying G(F_v) with GL_n x GL_n.

nodes.name: Nonvanishing of local zeta integrals
nodes.statement:
Let $v$ be a place of $F$. 
    Then there exists $W_v \in \mathcal W(\Pi_v, \psi_{L_v})$ and $\phi_v' \in \mathcal S(E_{v,n})$    such that 
    $\lambda_v(\frac12, W_v, \mu_v, \phi_v') \neq 0$.
conclusions: there exists $W_v \in \mathcal W(\Pi_v, \psi_{L_v})$ and $\phi_v' \in \mathcal S(E_{v,n})$ such that $\lambda_v(\frac12, W_v, \mu_v, \phi_v') \neq 0$
nodes.label: lem:archgood

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.4.8
nodes.statement: The case when $\mu$ is trivial is proved in \cite[Lemma 3.3.3]{BP21} or \cite{Yadav2025}. The same proof applied to the case when $\mu$ is not trivial.
nodes.statement_short: As in Beuzart-Plessis (or Yadav) for trivial mu; same proof for general mu.

nodes.name: Local distributions agree at E-split places
nodes.statement:
Let $v$ be a place of $F$ that is split in $E$. 
There is a nonzero 
constant $c$ such that 
\[
    I_{\Pi_v}(\tfrac12, f'_v, \phi_v')
    = c J_{\pi_v}(f_v, \phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v})
\]
for all matching test functions $(f_v', \phi_v')$
and $(f_v, \phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v})$.
assumptions: Let $v$ be a place of $F$ that is split in $E$.
conclusions: There is a nonzero constant $c$ such that \[ I_{\Pi_v}(\tfrac12, f'_v, \phi_v') = c J_{\pi_v}(f_v, \phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v}) \] for all matching test functions $(f_v', \phi_v')$ and $(f_v, \phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v})$.
nodes.label: lem:splitlocaldistrid

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.4.9
nodes.statement:
Since $v$ is split in $E$, we have $L_v = K_v \times K_v$.
Then $\pi_v$ is a representation of
$\mathrm{GL}_n(K_v)$, and $\Pi_v = \pi_v \otimes \pi_v^\vee$
is a representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(K_v) \times \mathrm{GL}_n(K_v)$.
Identify $\mathbb L$ with $F_n$ as in Section 
\ref{sec:splittransfer}.
By the definition of matching at a split place given
in Proposition \ref{prop:splittransfer}, we have
\[
    f_{1,v}' \ast f_{2,v}'^\vee = f_v , \quad
    \phi_v' = \phi_{1,v} \otimes \overline{\phi_{2,v}}
\]
where $f_v \in C_c^\infty(\mathrm{GL}_n(K_v))$,
$\phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v} \in \mathcal S(F_n)\otimes
\mathcal S(F_n)$, $f_v' = f_{1,v}' \otimes f_{2,v}' 
\in C_c^\infty(\mathrm{GL}_n(K_v) \times \mathrm{GL}_n(K_v))$,
and $\phi_v' \in \mathcal S(F_n \times F_n)$.

Let $\psi_{K_v}$ be the additive character of $K_v$
given by
\[
    \psi_{K_v}(x) = \psi_{F_v}(j_K(x - \sigma_{K/F}(x))).
\]
Note that $\psi_{L_v}(x, y) = \psi_{K_v}(x)\psi_{K_v}(y)$.
Suppose $j_M = (j_0, -j_0) \in K \times K$, where
$j_0 \in K$.
Let 
\[
    \psi_{L_v}'(x, y) = \psi_{L_v}(j_0x, -j_0y).
\]
Then $\psi_{L_v}'(x, y) = \psi_{K_v}'(x)
\overline{\psi_{K_v}'(y)}$, where
$\psi_{K_v}'(x) = \psi_{K_v}(j_0x)$.

For $W_v \in \mathcal W(\Pi_v, \psi_{L_v})$, let
\[
    W_v'(g) \coloneqq W_v\left(\begin{pmatrix}
    \epsilon_{n-1} & \\ & 1
    \end{pmatrix} g\right).
\]
Then $W_v' \in \mathcal W(\Pi_v, \psi_{L_v}')
= \mathcal W(\pi_v, \psi_{K_v}') \otimes 
\overline{\mathcal W(\pi_v, \psi_{K_v}')}$. 
Suppose $W_v' = W_{1,v}' \otimes \overline{W_{2,v}'}$
for $W_{1,v}', W_{2,v}' \in \mathcal W(\pi_v, \psi_{K_v}')$.
Then we have
\[
    \beta_v(W_v) = \langle W_{1,v}', W_{2,v}' \rangle_v
\]
and
\[
    \langle W_v, W_v \rangle_v =
    \langle W_{1,v}', W_{1,v}'\rangle_v
    \langle W_{2,v}', W_{2,v}'\rangle_v.
\]
By \cite[Theorem~B]{Sun2012multiplicity}, the space
\[
    \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{GL}_n(F_v) \times \mathrm{GL}_n(F_v)}(\pi_v 
    \otimes \overline{\omega_v} 
    \otimes \overline{\pi_v}
    \otimes \omega_v, \mathbb C)
\]
has dimension $1$.
Thus, there exists a nonzero constant $c$ such that
\[
    \lambda_v(\tfrac12, \Pi_v(f_v')W_v, \mu_v, \phi_{1,v}
    \otimes \overline{\phi_{2,v}})
    = c\cdot \ell_v(\pi_v(f_{1,v}')W_{1,v}', 
    \phi_{1,v})\overline{\ell_v(\pi_v(\overline{f_{2,v}'}) W_{2,v}',
    \phi_{2,v})}.
\]

Thus,
\begin{align*}
    I_{\Pi_v}(\tfrac12, f_v', \phi_v')
    &=
    c\sum_{W_{1,v}'} \ell_v(\pi_v(f_{1,v}')
    W_{1,v}', \phi_{1,v})
    \overline{\ell_v(\pi_v(\overline{f_{2,v}'})W_{1,v}', \phi_{2,v})} \\
    &= c\sum_{W_{1,v}'} \ell_v(\pi_v(f_{1,v}'
    \ast f_{2,v}'^\vee)
    W_{1,v}', \phi_{1,v})
    \overline{\ell_v(W_{1,v}', \phi_{2,v})}\\
    &= c\sum_{W_{1,v}'} \ell_v(\pi_v(f_{v})
    W_{1,v}', \phi_{1,v})
    \overline{\ell_v(W_{1,v}', \phi_{2,v})}\\
    &= cJ_{\pi_v}(f_v, \phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v}),
\end{align*}
where $W_{1,v}'$ runs over an orthonormal basis of
$\mathcal W(\pi_v, \psi_{K_v}')$.
nodes.statement_short: Identify Pi_v = pi_v x pi_v^vee and Whittaker models, use multiplicity one (Sun) to compare the zeta integral with ell_v x ell_v, then sum over a basis.

nodes.name: At an E-split place write Pi_v = pi_v x pi_v^vee and recall
nodes.statement:
Since $v$ is split in $E$, we have $L_v = K_v \times K_v$.
Then $\pi_v$ is a representation of
$\mathrm{GL}_n(K_v)$, and $\Pi_v = \pi_v \otimes \pi_v^\vee$
is a representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(K_v) \times \mathrm{GL}_n(K_v)$.
Identify $\mathbb L$ with $F_n$ as in Section 
\ref{sec:splittransfer}.
By the definition of matching at a split place given
in Proposition \ref{prop:splittransfer}, we have
\[
    f_{1,v}' \ast f_{2,v}'^\vee = f_v , \quad
    \phi_v' = \phi_{1,v} \otimes \overline{\phi_{2,v}}
\]
where $f_v \in C_c^\infty(\mathrm{GL}_n(K_v))$,
$\phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v} \in \mathcal S(F_n)\otimes
\mathcal S(F_n)$, $f_v' = f_{1,v}' \otimes f_{2,v}' 
\in C_c^\infty(\mathrm{GL}_n(K_v) \times \mathrm{GL}_n(K_v))$,
and $\phi_v' \in \mathcal S(F_n \times F_n)$.
nodes.statement_short: At an E-split place write Pi_v = pi_v x pi_v^vee and recall the split matching.

nodes.name: Introduce the twisted additive characters psi'_{K_v}, psi'_{
nodes.statement:
Let $\psi_{K_v}$ be the additive character of $K_v$
given by
\[
    \psi_{K_v}(x) = \psi_{F_v}(j_K(x - \sigma_{K/F}(x))).
\]
Note that $\psi_{L_v}(x, y) = \psi_{K_v}(x)\psi_{K_v}(y)$.
Suppose $j_M = (j_0, -j_0) \in K \times K$, where
$j_0 \in K$.
Let 
\[
    \psi_{L_v}'(x, y) = \psi_{L_v}(j_0x, -j_0y).
\]
Then $\psi_{L_v}'(x, y) = \psi_{K_v}'(x)
\overline{\psi_{K_v}'(y)}$, where
$\psi_{K_v}'(x) = \psi_{K_v}(j_0x)$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the twisted additive characters psi'_{K_v}, psi'_{L_v}.

nodes.name: Translate W_v to W_v' = W_1' x conj(W_2'); express beta_v an
nodes.statement:
For $W_v \in \mathcal W(\Pi_v, \psi_{L_v})$, let
\[
    W_v'(g) \coloneqq W_v\left(\begin{pmatrix}
    \epsilon_{n-1} & \\ & 1
    \end{pmatrix} g\right).
\]
Then $W_v' \in \mathcal W(\Pi_v, \psi_{L_v}')
= \mathcal W(\pi_v, \psi_{K_v}') \otimes 
\overline{\mathcal W(\pi_v, \psi_{K_v}')}$. 
Suppose $W_v' = W_{1,v}' \otimes \overline{W_{2,v}'}$
for $W_{1,v}', W_{2,v}' \in \mathcal W(\pi_v, \psi_{K_v}')$.
Then we have
\[
    \beta_v(W_v) = \langle W_{1,v}', W_{2,v}' \rangle_v
\]
and
\[
    \langle W_v, W_v \rangle_v =
    \langle W_{1,v}', W_{1,v}'\rangle_v
    \langle W_{2,v}', W_{2,v}'\rangle_v.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Translate W_v to W_v' = W_1' x conj(W_2'); express beta_v and norms.

nodes.name: Multiplicity one (Sun) gives lambda_v = c * ell_v x conj(ell
nodes.statement:
By \cite[Theorem~B]{Sun2012multiplicity}, the space
\[
    \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{GL}_n(F_v) \times \mathrm{GL}_n(F_v)}(\pi_v 
    \otimes \overline{\omega_v} 
    \otimes \overline{\pi_v}
    \otimes \omega_v, \mathbb C)
\]
has dimension $1$.
Thus, there exists a nonzero constant $c$ such that
\[
    \lambda_v(\tfrac12, \Pi_v(f_v')W_v, \mu_v, \phi_{1,v}
    \otimes \overline{\phi_{2,v}})
    = c\cdot \ell_v(\pi_v(f_{1,v}')W_{1,v}', 
    \phi_{1,v})\overline{\ell_v(\pi_v(\overline{f_{2,v}'}) W_{2,v}',
    \phi_{2,v})}.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Multiplicity one (Sun) gives lambda_v = c * ell_v x conj(ell_v).

nodes.name: Sum over a basis to get I_{Pi_v} = c J_{pi_v}.
nodes.statement:
Thus,
\begin{align*}
    I_{\Pi_v}(\tfrac12, f_v', \phi_v')
    &=
    c\sum_{W_{1,v}'} \ell_v(\pi_v(f_{1,v}')
    W_{1,v}', \phi_{1,v})
    \overline{\ell_v(\pi_v(\overline{f_{2,v}'})W_{1,v}', \phi_{2,v})} \\
    &= c\sum_{W_{1,v}'} \ell_v(\pi_v(f_{1,v}'
    \ast f_{2,v}'^\vee)
    W_{1,v}', \phi_{1,v})
    \overline{\ell_v(W_{1,v}', \phi_{2,v})}\\
    &= c\sum_{W_{1,v}'} \ell_v(\pi_v(f_{v})
    W_{1,v}', \phi_{1,v})
    \overline{\ell_v(W_{1,v}', \phi_{2,v})}\\
    &= cJ_{\pi_v}(f_v, \phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v}),
\end{align*}
where $W_{1,v}'$ runs over an orthonormal basis of
$\mathcal W(\pi_v, \psi_{K_v}')$.
nodes.statement_short: Sum over a basis to get I_{Pi_v} = c J_{pi_v}.

nodes.name: Asai representation As(phi_v)
nodes.statement:
Choose $s \in W_{E_v}' - W_{L_v}'$.
We define a representation $\mathrm{As}(\phi_v) \colon
W_{E_v}' \to \mathrm{GL}(M \otimes M)$ by
\[
    \mathrm{As}(\phi_v)(w) = \phi_v(w) \otimes \phi_v(sws^{-1}), \; w \in W_{E_v}', 
\]
\[
    \mathrm{As}(\phi_v)(s)(m_1 \otimes m_2) = m_2 \otimes
    \phi_v(s^2)(m_1), \; m_1 \otimes m_2 \in M \otimes M.
\]

nodes.name: Local Asai L-factor (field case)
nodes.statement:
We define the local Asai $L$-factor 
\[
    L(s, \Pi_v, \mathrm{As}_{L_v/E_v}) \coloneqq
    L(s, \mathrm{As}(\phi_v))
\]
where $L(s, \mathrm{As}(\phi_v))$ is the local $L$-factor
associated to $\mathrm{As}(\phi_v)$ as in
\cite[Section~3]{MR546607} and \cite[Section~2.2]{MR2730575}.

nodes.name: Local Asai L-factor (split case)
nodes.statement:
Secondly, assume that $L_v = E_v \times E_v$ is split. Then
$\Pi_v = \Pi_{1,v} \boxtimes \Pi_{2,v}$ for some
irreducible representations $\Pi_{1,v}$ and $\Pi_{2,v}$
of $\mathrm{GL}_n(E_v)$.
Let
\[
    L(s, \Pi_v, \mathrm{As}_{L_v/E_v})
    \coloneqq L(s, \Pi_{1,v} \times \Pi_{2,v})
    = L(s, \phi_{1,v} \otimes \phi_{2,v}),
\]
where $\phi_{1,v}$ and $\phi_{2,v}$ are the admissible
representations of $W_{E_v}'$ associated to
$\Pi_{1,v}$ and $\Pi_{2,v}$ by the local Langlands
correspondence.

nodes.name: Twisted local Asai L-factor
nodes.statement:
We also define the
twisted local Asai $L$-factor
\[
    L(s, \Pi_v, \mathrm{As}_{L_v/E_v} \times \mu_v)
    \coloneqq L(s, \mathrm{As}(\phi_v) \otimes \mu_v)
\]
if $L_v$ is a field, and
\[
    L(s, \Pi_v, \mathrm{As}_{L_v/E_v} \times \mu_v)
    \coloneqq L(s, \Pi_{1,v} \times \Pi_{2,v}
    \otimes \mu_v)
\]
if $L_v = E_v \times E_v$.

nodes.name: Global twisted Asai L-function
nodes.statement:
Define the global twisted Asai L-function $(s \in \mathbb C)$
\[
    L(s, \Pi, \mathrm{As}_{L/E} \times \mu) = \prod_{v}
    L(s, \Pi_v, \mathrm{As}_{L_v/E_v} \times \mu_v),
\]
where $v$ runs over all places $v$ of $E$.
This product is absolutely convergent for
$\textnormal{Re}(s)$ sufficiently large.

nodes.name: Zeta integral characterization of the central Asai L-value
nodes.statement:
There exists $\varphi \in \Pi$ and
$\phi' \in \mathcal S(\mathbb A_{E,n})$ such that
$\lambda(\frac12, \varphi, \mu, \phi') \neq 0$
if and only if $L(\frac12, \Pi, \mathrm{As}_{L/E}\times
\mu^{-1}) \neq 0$.
conclusions: There exists $\varphi \in \Pi$ and $\phi' \in \mathcal S(\mathbb A_{E,n})$ such that $\lambda(\frac12, \varphi, \mu, \phi') \neq 0$ if and only if $L(\frac12, \Pi, \mathrm{As}_{L/E}\times \mu^{-1}) \neq 0$.
equivalent_conditions: There exists $\varphi \in \Pi$ and $\phi' \in \mathcal S(\mathbb A_{E,n})$ such that $\lambda(\frac12, \varphi, \mu, \phi') \neq 0$
nodes.label: thm:asai

nodes.name: Proof that (2) implies (1)
nodes.statement:
Assume that the period integral $\mathcal P$ is not 
identically zero for some skew-Hermitian space $V$
and a cuspidal automorphic representation
$\pi$ of $\mathrm{U}(V)(\mathbb A_K)$ such that $\operatorname{BC}
(\pi) = \Pi$.

By Theorem \ref{thm:asai}, in order to show
that $L(\frac{1}{2}, \Pi, \mathrm{As}_{L/E} \times \mu^{-1})$ is 
nonzero, it suffices to show there exists a test
function $(f', \phi')$ such that
\[ I_\Pi(f', \phi') \neq 0.\]
To show that such a test function exists,
we first find a test function 
$(f, \phi) \in C_c^\infty(G(\mathbb A)) \times 
\mathcal S(\mathbb L(\mathbb A))^{\otimes 2}$ which is good
in the sense of Definition \ref{def:ugood}
such that 
\[ J_\pi(f, \phi) \neq 0.\] 
Suppose $\mathcal P(\varphi, \widetilde\phi_0) \neq 0$ for some factorizable
$\varphi \in \pi$ and $\widetilde \phi_0 \in \mathcal S(\mathbb L(\mathbb A))$.
By \eqref{eq:postype}, this
implies there exists a factorizable test 
function $(\widetilde f, \widetilde\phi)$ of 
positive type, with $\widetilde\phi = \widetilde\phi_0 \otimes
\widetilde\phi_0$,
such that $J_\pi(\widetilde f, \widetilde\phi) \neq 
0$.

We define a good test function 
\[
    (f, \phi) = (\otimes_v f_v, \otimes_v \phi_v)
\]
by modifying $(\widetilde f, \widetilde\phi)$ at certain
places as follows. In the process, we also
define a constant $k$ which will be used for choosing 
$k$-Kottwitz representatives.

Recall that $v_1$ and $v_2$ are two nonarchimedean
places of $F$ which are completely split in $L$,
such that $\pi_{v_1}$ and $\pi_{v_2}$ are
supercuspidal.

Let $\Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$ be the set of places $v$
of $F$ which are inert in $E$ and unramified
in $K$, such that
$\mu_v, \psi_v'$ are unramified,
$j \in \mathcal O_{E_v}^\times$, and $\Pi_v$ (and thus 
$\pi_v$) is unramified.

Let $\{v_3, \dots, v_m\}$ be the set of places of $v$
of $F$ such that $v \not\in \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$
and $v$ is not split in $E$.
By assumptions \eqref{item:fieldsunr},
\eqref{item:charsunr}, and \eqref{item:piunr} of
the theorem, this set
is finite and all elements are split in $K$.

As $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{U}(V)(F_v)}(\pi_v \otimes \overline{\omega_{\psi_v',
\mu_v}}, \mathbb C) \neq 0$ 
for all $v$, the local twisted GGP 
conjecture \cite{le2025local} tells us that $V$ is the
split skew-Hermitian space at all $v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$.
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item For all $v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$, let
$(f_v, \phi_v)$ be the unramified
test function specified in Section \ref{sec:FL}. 
Since $\pi_v$ is unramified,
we have $J_{\pi_v}(f_v, \phi_v) \neq 0$.

\item 
Let $(f_{v_1}, \phi_{v_1})$
be a test function such that
$J_{\pi_{v_1}}(f_{v_1}, \phi_{v_1}) \neq 0$ and 
$f_{v_1}$ is a truncated matrix coefficient of a 
supercuspidal representation. 
Such a test function exists
by Lemma \ref{lem:matrixcoeff}, 
since $\Pi_{v_1}$ is supercuspidal, so
$\pi_{v_1}$ is also supercuspidal.

\item Let $(f_{v_2}, \phi_{v_2})$ be a test function
and let $k \ge 0$ be an integer such that 
$J_{\pi_{v_2}}(f_{v_2}, \phi_{v_2}) \neq 0$, and
the regular semisimple support condition of Definition
\ref{def:ugood} \eqref{ursssupp}
is satisfied for all $k$-Kottwitz 
sets of representatives $R^V$.
These exist by Lemma \ref{lem:rsssupp}.

By Proposition \ref{prop:Ksplittransfer},
we can also assume $k$ is large enough so that
for $3 \le i \le m$, there exists a test function
$(f_{v_i}', \phi_{v_i}')$ on the general linear
side, which is a smooth
transfer of $(\widetilde f_{v_i}, \widetilde \phi_{v_i})$ for all
$k$-Kottwitz sets of representatives $S$
and $R^V$.

\item For all $v \not\in \{v_1, v_2\} \cup
\Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$, let $(f_v, \phi_{v}) = 
(\widetilde f_v, \widetilde\phi_v)$. Note that all such $v$
are either split in $E$ or an element of
$\{v_3, \dots, v_m\}$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $S$ and $R^V$ be compatible sets of global
representatives such that each element of $S$ 
or $R^V$ is Kottwitz at all places of $F$ which
are inert in $E$, 
and $k$-Kottwitz at $v_2, \dots, v_m$.
Such a choice of representatives exists by
Proposition \ref{prop:globalkottwitz}.
Let $(f', \phi')$ be a smooth transfer, as
defined in Definition \ref{defn: global smooth transfer},
of the collection of test functions
\[
    \{(f^{V'}, \phi^{V'} )\}_{V' \in [\mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)]}
\]
where $(f^{V'}, \phi^{V'}) = 0$ 
for $V' \not\simeq V$ and $(f^{V}, \phi^{V}) = (f, \phi)$.
Because $(f_v, \phi_{v})$ is the unramified test 
function at all $v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$, such 
transfer $(f',\phi')$ exist by
Propositions \ref{prop:FL}, \ref{prop:splittransfer}, 
and \ref{prop:Ksplittransfer}.

Then $(f', \phi')$ is also good, so by
Proposition \ref{prop:identity}, 
\begin{align*}
    I_\Pi(f', \phi') 
    &= \sum_{\operatorname{BC}(\pi') = \Pi} J_{\pi'}(f, \phi) 
    \\&= 
    J_{\pi_{v_1}}(f_{v_1},\phi_{v_1})\cdot
    J_{\pi_{v_2}}(f_{v_2}, \phi_{v_2})
    \sum_{\operatorname{BC}(\pi') = \Pi}
    \prod_{v \ne v_1, v_2}
    J_{\pi_v'}(f_v, \phi_v).
\end{align*}
Note that each of the terms in the
sum on the second line is nonnegative because 
$(f_v, \phi_v)$ is of
positive type for $v \neq v_1, v_2$.
Furthermore,
\[
    \prod_{v \neq v_1, v_2} J_{\pi_v}(f_v, \phi_v)
    = \prod_{v \neq v_1, v_2}
    J_{\pi_v}(\widetilde f_v, \widetilde \phi_v) \cdot 
    \prod_{v \text{ inert in } E}
    \frac{J_{\pi_v}(f_v, \phi_v)}
    {J_{\pi_v}(\widetilde f_v, \widetilde\phi_v)} \neq 0
\]
since $J_{\pi}(\widetilde f, \widetilde \phi) \neq 0$ by assumption,
and the product over inert places is a finite
product of nonzero terms.
Thus, the term corresponding to $\pi$ in the sum is
nonzero, so $I_{\Pi}(f', \phi') \neq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: From a nonzero period build a good positive-type unitary test function with nonzero J_pi, transfer it to the GL side, and use the relative trace identity plus positivity to get I_Pi != 0, hence L(1/2) != 0. nodes.name: Proof that (1) implies (2)
nodes.statement:
\leavevmode
By Theorem \ref{thm:asai},
$L(\frac{1}{2}, \Pi, \mathrm{As}_{L/E} \times \mu^{-1}) \neq 0$ 
implies that there exists 
$\varphi \in \Pi$, $\widetilde \phi' \in \mathcal S(\mathbb A_{E,n})$ such that
\[
    \lambda(\tfrac12, \varphi, \mu, \widetilde \phi') \neq 0.
\]
Furthermore, for each archimedean place $v$ of $F$,
by Lemma \ref{lem:archgood} applied
to the extension $K/F$, we can assume that
the function $\widetilde\phi_v'$ is 
of the form
$\phi_{1,v}' \otimes \phi_{2, v}'$ where
$\phi_{1,v}', \phi_{2,v}' \in \mathcal S(F_{v,n})$.
Since $\Pi$ is Hermitian, by \cite{MR1344660}, 
there also exists 
$\varphi' \in \Pi$ such that $\beta(\varphi') \neq 0$.
Thus, there exists factorizable $\widetilde f'$
such that 
\[
    I_\Pi(\widetilde f', \widetilde \phi') \neq 0.
\]

As before, we define a test function
\[
    (f', \phi') = (\otimes_v f'_v, \otimes_v \phi_v'),
\]
which is good in the sense of 
Definition \ref{def:glgood}, by modifying 
$(\widetilde f', \widetilde\phi')$.
Let $\Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$ and $\{v_3, \dots, v_m\}$ 
be as in the proof of (2) implies (1).
As before, we will also define a constant $k$ used
for choosing $k$-Kottwitz representatives.
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item
For all $v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$,
let $(f_v', \phi_v')$ be the unramified test function.
Since $\Pi_v$ is unramified, we have
$I_{\Pi_v}(f_v', \phi_v') \neq 0$.

\item By Lemma \ref{lem:splitlocaldistrid}, $I_{\Pi_v}(f_v', \phi_v') \neq 0$ implies that
$J_{\pi_v}$ is nonzero for every place
of $F$ which is split in $E$.
Thus by Lemma \ref{lem:matrixcoeff}, there exists
a test function $(f_{v_1}, \phi_{v_1})$
on the unitary side such that
$J_{\pi_{v_1}}(f_{v_1}, \phi_{v_1}) \neq 0$ and 
$f_{v_1}$ is a
truncated matrix coefficient of a supercuspidal
representation.
Let $(f_{v_1}', \phi_{v_1}')$ be the smooth transfer
of $(f_{v_1}, \phi_{v_1})$.

\item By Lemma \ref{lem:rsssupp}, 
there exists a test function $(f_{v_2}, \phi_{v_2})$
on the unitary side and an integer $k \ge 0$ such
that $J_{\pi_{v_2}}(f_{v_2}, \phi_{v_2}) \neq 0$
and condition \eqref{ursssupp} of Definition
\ref{def:ugood} is satisfied for all $k$-Kottwitz
sets of representatives $R^V$.
Let $(f_{v_2}', \phi_{v_2}')$ be the smooth transfer
of $(f_{v_2}, \phi_{v_2})$.

By Proposition \ref{prop:Ksplittransfer},
we can suppose $k$ is large enough so that for $3 \le i \le m$,
there exists a test function $(f_{v_i}, \phi_{v_i})$
on the unitary side which is a smooth transfer
of $(\widetilde f_{v_i}', \widetilde \phi_{v_i}')$ for all $k$-Kottwitz
sets of representatives $S$ and $R^V$.

\item For all $v \not\in \{v_1, v_2\}
\cup \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$, let $(f_v', \phi_v') = (\widetilde f_v', \widetilde \phi_v')$.
\end{enumerate}



Let $S$ and $R^V$ be compatible sets
of representatives which are Kottwitz at all inert
places and $k$-Kottwitz at $v_2, \dots, v_m$.
Let 
\[
    \{(f^V, \phi^V)\}_{V \in [\mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)]}
\] 
be a smooth transfer of $(f', \phi')$ as
in Definition \ref{defn: global smooth transfer}. 
Such a transfer exists locally at each place
by Propositions \ref{prop:FL}, 
\ref{prop:splittransfer}, and 
\ref{prop:Ksplittransfer}.

Then Proposition \ref{prop:identity} tells us that
\[
    I_\Pi(f', \phi') 
    = \sum_{V}
    \sum_{\operatorname{BC}(\pi) = \Pi} J_{\pi}(f^{V}, \phi^{V}) \neq 0.
\]
This implies that the period integral
$\mathcal P$ is nonzero for some skew-Hermitian space $V$ over $E$ and
some $\pi$ such that $\operatorname{BC}(\pi) = \Pi$.
nodes.statement_short: From L(1/2) != 0 get a nonzero zeta integral and Flicker--Rallis period, build a good GL test function with I_Pi != 0, transfer to the unitary side, and conclude via the relative trace identity.

As before, we define a test function
\[
    (f', \phi') = (\otimes_v f'_v, \otimes_v \phi_v'),
\]
which is good in the sense of 
Definition \ref{def:glgood}, by modifying 
$(\widetilde f', \widetilde\phi')$.
Let $\Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$ and $\{v_3, \dots, v_m\}$ 
be as in the proof of (2) implies (1).
As before, we will also define a constant $k$ used
for choosing $k$-Kottwitz representatives.
nodes.statement_short: Modify (f~',phi~') at finitely many places; reuse Sigma_in, v_3..v_m and define k.

nodes.name: At Sigma_in use the unramified test function.
nodes.statement:
For all $v \in \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$,
let $(f_v', \phi_v')$ be the unramified test function.
Since $\Pi_v$ is unramified, we have
$I_{\Pi_v}(f_v', \phi_v') \neq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: At Sigma_in use the unramified test function.

nodes.name: At v_1 use Lemmas 5.4.9 and 5.4.6 and transfer.
nodes.statement:
By Lemma \ref{lem:splitlocaldistrid}, $I_{\Pi_v}(f_v', \phi_v') \neq 0$ implies that
$J_{\pi_v}$ is nonzero for every place
of $F$ which is split in $E$.
Thus by Lemma \ref{lem:matrixcoeff}, there exists
a test function $(f_{v_1}, \phi_{v_1})$
on the unitary side such that
$J_{\pi_{v_1}}(f_{v_1}, \phi_{v_1}) \neq 0$ and 
$f_{v_1}$ is a
truncated matrix coefficient of a supercuspidal
representation.
Let $(f_{v_1}', \phi_{v_1}')$ be the smooth transfer
of $(f_{v_1}, \phi_{v_1})$.
nodes.statement_short: At v_1 use Lemmas 5.4.9 and 5.4.6 and transfer.

nodes.name: At v_2 use Lemma 5.4.7, choose k large, and transfer.
nodes.statement:
By Lemma \ref{lem:rsssupp}, 
there exists a test function $(f_{v_2}, \phi_{v_2})$
on the unitary side and an integer $k \ge 0$ such
that $J_{\pi_{v_2}}(f_{v_2}, \phi_{v_2}) \neq 0$
and condition \eqref{ursssupp} of Definition
\ref{def:ugood} is satisfied for all $k$-Kottwitz
sets of representatives $R^V$.
Let $(f_{v_2}', \phi_{v_2}')$ be the smooth transfer
of $(f_{v_2}, \phi_{v_2})$.

By Proposition \ref{prop:Ksplittransfer},
we can suppose $k$ is large enough so that for $3 \le i \le m$,
there exists a test function $(f_{v_i}, \phi_{v_i})$
on the unitary side which is a smooth transfer
of $(\widetilde f_{v_i}', \widetilde \phi_{v_i}')$ for all $k$-Kottwitz
sets of representatives $S$ and $R^V$.
nodes.statement_short: At v_2 use Lemma 5.4.7, choose k large, and transfer.

nodes.name: Elsewhere keep the original test function.
nodes.statement:
For all $v \not\in \{v_1, v_2\}
\cup \Sigma_{\textnormal{in}}$, let $(f_v', \phi_v') = (\widetilde f_v', \widetilde \phi_v')$.
nodes.statement_short: Elsewhere keep the original test function.

nodes.name: Choose compatible representatives and a unitary smooth trans
nodes.statement:
Let $S$ and $R^V$ be compatible sets
of representatives which are Kottwitz at all inert
places and $k$-Kottwitz at $v_2, \dots, v_m$.
Let 
\[
    \{(f^V, \phi^V)\}_{V \in [\mathrm{SHerm}_n^\times(F)]}
\] 
be a smooth transfer of $(f', \phi')$ as
in Definition \ref{defn: global smooth transfer}. 
Such a transfer exists locally at each place
by Propositions \ref{prop:FL}, 
\ref{prop:splittransfer}, and 
\ref{prop:Ksplittransfer}.
nodes.statement_short: Choose compatible representatives and a unitary smooth transfer (Props. 4.2.3, 4.3.2, 4.4.5).

nodes.name: The relative trace identity gives a nonzero unitary spectral
nodes.statement:
Then Proposition \ref{prop:identity} tells us that
\[
    I_\Pi(f', \phi') 
    = \sum_{V}
    \sum_{\operatorname{BC}(\pi) = \Pi} J_{\pi}(f^{V}, \phi^{V}) \neq 0.
\]
This implies that the period integral
$\mathcal P$ is nonzero for some skew-Hermitian space $V$ over $E$ and
some $\pi$ such that $\operatorname{BC}(\pi) = \Pi$.
nodes.statement_short: The relative trace identity gives a nonzero unitary spectral term, so the period is nonzero.
